tasks.title: LRU cache class
tasks.user_request: Write an LRUCache class in Python with `get(key)` and `put(key, value)` that holds at most `capacity` items and evicts the least recently used one when full. `get` on a missing key should return None. Please include a pytest file for it.
tasks.clean_requirements: Implementation must track recency on both get and put (an existing key updated via put becomes most-recent), evict the least recently used entry when inserting beyond capacity, and return None for missing keys. Tests must assert: basic put/get roundtrip; eviction of the oldest key after exceeding capacity; that a `get` refreshes recency so a different key gets evicted; that updating an existing key via `put` refreshes recency and overwrites the value without growing size; capacity of 1 behaves correctly; and `get` on a missing/evicted key returns None. Tests must compare actual returned values, not just call methods.
tasks.failure_stakes: A cache that evicts the wrong entry or fails to refresh on access silently destroys hit rate in production, and tests that only check 'no exception' will never catch it.

tasks.title: Merge overlapping intervals
tasks.user_request: I need a function `merge_intervals(intervals: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]` that merges any overlapping or touching intervals and returns them sorted. Can you write it plus pytest tests?
tasks.clean_requirements: Function must sort by start, merge intervals where next.start <= current.end (touching intervals like (1,3),(3,5) merge to (1,5)), and handle unsorted input. Tests must assert exact output lists for: empty input returns []; single interval returned unchanged; two non-overlapping intervals stay separate and sorted; overlapping intervals merge; touching intervals merge; one interval fully containing another collapses to the outer; a chain of three intervals merging into one; unsorted input produces sorted merged output; duplicate intervals collapse to one. Tests must not mutate-check only or assert merely that a list is returned.
tasks.failure_stakes: Off-by-one at interval boundaries (touching vs. overlapping) leads to double-booked calendar slots or gaps in time-range coverage that no one notices until users complain.

tasks.title: Fixed-size ring buffer
tasks.user_request: Implement a RingBuffer(capacity) class with `append(item)`, `pop()` (oldest first), `__len__`, and `to_list()`. When full, append should overwrite the oldest item. Add pytest tests too.
tasks.clean_requirements: Buffer must maintain FIFO order, overwrite the oldest element when at capacity, keep len() capped at capacity, raise an error (e.g. IndexError) on pop from empty, and have to_list() return items oldest-to-newest. Tests must assert: empty buffer has len 0 and to_list() == []; appending fewer than capacity preserves order; appending exactly capacity items fills it; appending beyond capacity drops the oldest and to_list() reflects it; pop returns oldest and reduces len; pop on empty raises; interleaved append/pop across the wraparound point still yields correct order; capacity of 1 works.
tasks.failure_stakes: A wraparound index bug returns stale or out-of-order samples, corrupting whatever metrics or log tail the buffer is feeding.

tasks.title: Min-stack with O(1) minimum
tasks.user_request: Write a MinStack class supporting push, pop, peek, and get_min, where get_min returns the current minimum in O(1). Include pytest tests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Implementation must keep an auxiliary min structure so get_min stays correct after pops. Tests must assert: get_min after a sequence of pushes equals the actual minimum; after popping the current minimum, get_min reverts to the previous minimum; duplicate minimum values are handled (push 1, push 1, pop → get_min still 1); peek returns top without removing; pop returns the removed value; pop/peek/get_min on an empty stack raise (e.g. IndexError); pushing a value larger than the current min doesn't change get_min. Tests must check concrete values, not just that methods run.
tasks.failure_stakes: A min-tracking bug that only shows up after pops returns a wrong minimum while appearing to work in happy-path demos.

tasks.title: Sliding window moving average
tasks.user_request: Create a `MovingAverage(window_size)` class with a `next(value) -> float` method that returns the average of the last `window_size` values seen so far (or of all values if fewer have been added). Write pytest tests for it.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must use a bounded deque or equivalent and a running sum so old values are dropped once the window is full. Tests must assert exact (or pytest.approx) averages: first value returns itself; averages during warm-up use only values seen so far; once full, the oldest value drops out and the average reflects only the last N; window_size of 1 returns the latest value each time; negative and float values work; window_size <= 0 raises ValueError. Tests must assert numeric return values from each `next` call.
tasks.failure_stakes: If old values don't fall out of the window, the 'moving' average becomes a cumulative average and every dashboard built on it is quietly wrong.

tasks.title: Insert interval into sorted list
tasks.user_request: Given a list of non-overlapping intervals sorted by start, write `insert_interval(intervals, new) -> list` that inserts `new`, merging anything it overlaps, and returns the still-sorted, non-overlapping result. Please add a pytest test module.
tasks.clean_requirements: Function must not mutate the input list, must place the new interval in sorted position, and merge all intervals it overlaps or touches. Tests must assert exact results for: inserting into an empty list; new interval before all existing (no overlap); after all existing; strictly between two intervals with no overlap; overlapping one interval; overlapping several consecutive intervals which collapse into one; new interval fully inside an existing one leaves list unchanged; new interval covering everything collapses to a single interval; touching boundaries merge; and that the original input list is unchanged after the call.
tasks.failure_stakes: A wrong merge when the new interval spans several existing ones produces overlapping ranges downstream, breaking any code that assumes the invariant holds.

tasks.title: Prefix trie
tasks.user_request: Implement a Trie class with `insert(word)`, `contains(word) -> bool`, and `words_with_prefix(prefix) -> list[str]` (sorted). Write pytest tests covering it.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must distinguish full words from mere prefixes (inserting 'apple' must not make contains('app') true), and words_with_prefix must return all complete words under the prefix sorted. Tests must assert: contains returns True for inserted word and False for a prefix of it; False for unrelated/missing words; words_with_prefix returns sorted list of matches, [] for a prefix with no matches, and all words for empty-string prefix; inserting the same word twice yields it once in results; a word that is a prefix of another (insert 'app' and 'apple') makes both contains calls True and both appear under prefix 'ap'; empty trie returns False / [].
tasks.failure_stakes: Confusing prefix nodes with terminal words means autocomplete returns garbage partial strings or reports nonexistent entries as present.

tasks.title: Top-K tracker
tasks.user_request: I want a `TopK(k)` class where I can call `add(item, score)` repeatedly and `get_top() -> list[tuple[item, score]]` returns the k highest-scoring items in descending score order. Use a heap. Include pytest tests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must retain only the k best items using a size-bounded min-heap (or equivalent), and get_top must return items in descending score. Tests must assert exact output for: fewer than k items added returns all of them sorted descending; exactly k items; more than k items drops the lowest scores; items added in random order still produce correct descending result; ties in score keep k items total (deterministic tie-break documented and tested); re-adding the same item with a higher score updates rather than duplicates, or the behavior is explicitly defined and tested; k <= 0 raises ValueError; get_top on empty returns [].
tasks.failure_stakes: A heap comparison bug or wrong heap polarity silently keeps the worst k items instead of the best, inverting a leaderboard or ranking feature.

tasks.title: Union-Find with path compression
tasks.user_request: Write a DisjointSet class with `find(x)`, `union(a, b)`, `connected(a, b)`, and a `component_count` property, creating elements lazily on first use. Add a pytest suite.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must implement find with path compression and union by rank/size, update component_count correctly (new element increments it, successful union decrements it, redundant union does not). Tests must assert: connected(a,b) is False before union and True after; transitivity (union a-b, union b-c → connected(a,c)); union of already-connected elements returns False/no-op and leaves component_count unchanged; find returns the same root for all members of a component; component_count equals number of distinct groups after a sequence of operations; connected(x,x) is True; lazily created singleton increments component_count.
tasks.failure_stakes: A broken union leaves components incorrectly split or merged, so dedup/clustering/graph-connectivity logic built on it gives wrong answers under load.

tasks.title: TTL cache with injectable clock
tasks.user_request: Implement a `TTLCache(ttl_seconds, clock=time.monotonic)` with `set(key, value)` and `get(key)` that returns None once an entry is older than the TTL. Please make the clock injectable so it's testable, and write pytest tests using a fake clock.
tasks.clean_requirements: Entries must store insertion time via the injected clock; get must return None (and ideally purge) for expired entries; set on an existing key must reset its timestamp. Tests must use a controllable fake clock (not sleep) and assert: get right after set returns the value; get at exactly ttl boundary follows the documented rule (e.g. expired when age >= ttl) and is tested at both sides of the boundary; get after expiry returns None; re-setting a key refreshes its expiry so it survives past the original deadline; get of a never-set key returns None; multiple keys with different insert times expire independently; ttl_seconds <= 0 raises ValueError.
tasks.failure_stakes: An off-by-one at the expiry boundary or a timestamp that isn't refreshed on overwrite serves stale data or needlessly evicts fresh data, and sleep-based tests would be too slow and flaky to catch it.

tasks.title: Email address validator
tasks.user_request: Can you write `is_valid_email(addr: str) -> bool` for a signup form? Doesn't need full RFC 5322, just the practical rules: one @, non-empty local part under 64 chars, domain with at least one dot and valid label characters, no leading/trailing dots or consecutive dots. Please add pytest tests too.
tasks.clean_requirements: Function returns True for normal addresses (user@example.com, first.last+tag@sub.example.co.uk) and False for: empty string, missing @, multiple @, empty local part, local part > 64 chars, leading/trailing dot in local part, consecutive dots (a..b@x.com), domain without a dot, domain labels with underscores/spaces/leading or trailing hyphens, TLD shorter than 2 chars, and non-str input (TypeError or False, but tests must pin one). Tests must assert both True and False cases individually rather than just that the call does not raise.
tasks.failure_stakes: Bad addresses get accepted into the user database and the team can't tell because the tests only check the function runs.

tasks.title: Config dict validator with required keys and types
tasks.user_request: I load app config from JSON into a dict and want `validate_config(cfg: dict, schema: dict) -> list[str]` where schema maps key -> (type, required: bool). It should return a list of human-readable error strings (empty list means valid). Include tests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Returns [] for a config that satisfies the schema. Returns one error per problem: missing required key ('missing required key: port'), wrong type ('port: expected int, got str'), and unknown keys not in schema. Optional keys may be absent without error. bool must not satisfy int (since bool is a subclass of int in Python) — tests must check this. Order of errors should be deterministic (e.g., schema order then unknown keys). Tests must assert exact error strings or at least the key names in each message, and the empty-list case.
tasks.failure_stakes: A misconfigured deployment (e.g. port given as a string) passes validation and the service crashes at runtime instead of at startup.

tasks.title: Semantic version string parser
tasks.user_request: Write `parse_semver(s: str) -> tuple[int, int, int, str | None]` that validates and parses strings like `1.2.3` or `1.2.3-beta.1` per semver 2.0 (major.minor.patch, optional prerelease, no build metadata needed). Raise ValueError on bad input. Tests please.
tasks.clean_requirements: Accepts X.Y.Z with non-negative integers and optional -prerelease (dot-separated alphanumeric/hyphen identifiers). Rejects with ValueError: leading zeros ('01.2.3'), negative numbers, missing components ('1.2'), extra components ('1.2.3.4'), leading 'v', empty prerelease ('1.2.3-'), empty prerelease identifier ('1.2.3-a..b'), whitespace, and empty string. Tests must use pytest.raises for each rejection class and assert exact tuples for accepted inputs including the None prerelease case.
tasks.failure_stakes: The release tooling accepts malformed version tags and publishes packages with versions that other tools cannot sort or compare.

tasks.title: Environment variable loader with type coercion
tasks.user_request: I want a helper `load_env(spec: dict[str, type], env: Mapping[str, str] | None = None) -> dict` that reads env vars (default os.environ), coerces to int/float/bool/str per the spec, and raises a `MissingEnvError` listing all missing names at once. Bools should accept true/false/1/0/yes/no case-insensitively. Add tests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Returns a dict of coerced values. int/float coercion errors raise ValueError naming the variable. Bool parsing accepts 'true','True','1','yes','YES','false','0','no' and rejects 'maybe' with ValueError. All missing names are collected and reported in a single MissingEnvError (tests must check a case with two missing vars and assert both names appear). Tests must inject a dict as env rather than mutating os.environ, and cover the empty spec returning {}.
tasks.failure_stakes: A service starts with a silently wrong type (e.g. DEBUG='false' treated as truthy) or developers get only one missing-variable error at a time across many restarts.

tasks.title: ISO 8601 date string validator
tasks.user_request: Need `validate_date(s: str) -> date` that only accepts strict `YYYY-MM-DD` and returns a `datetime.date`, raising ValueError otherwise. Calendar correctness matters (Feb 30 should fail, leap years should work). Write pytest tests for it.
tasks.clean_requirements: Accepts '2024-02-29' (leap year), '2023-12-31', '0001-01-01'. Rejects: '2023-02-29' (non-leap), '2023-02-30', '2023-13-01', '2023-00-10', '2023-1-5' (unpadded), '20230105', '2023/01/05', '2023-01-05T00:00:00', trailing/leading whitespace, empty string. Tests must assert the returned date object equals the expected date and use pytest.raises(ValueError) for each invalid form, including the leap-year distinction.
tasks.failure_stakes: Invalid dates flow into the database or reports and cause downstream exceptions or silently wrong billing periods.

tasks.title: Nested schema checker with path-qualified errors
tasks.user_request: Write `check_schema(data, schema) -> list[str]` where schema is a nested structure: a Python type means 'value must be instance of', a dict means 'data must be a dict with these keys and sub-schemas', and a list of one schema means 'list where every item matches'. Errors should include the JSON-ish path like `users[2].email`. Tests included please.
tasks.clean_requirements: Returns [] when data fully matches. Reports a type mismatch with path and expected/actual types, a missing key with its path, and wrong container type (e.g. expected dict at 'users[0]' got str). Paths: root errors use '$' or empty, nested keys dot-joined, list indices in brackets. Must validate every list item and collect all errors rather than stopping at the first. Tests must assert the exact path strings for at least a nested-list-in-dict case, a top-level mismatch, an empty list (valid), and a multi-error case checking the count of errors.
tasks.failure_stakes: API payload bugs are reported with vague or wrong locations, costing developers time hunting the actual bad field in large payloads.

tasks.title: Password policy checker
tasks.user_request: Implement `check_password(pw: str, min_len: int = 12) -> list[str]` that returns the list of rule violations: too short, no uppercase, no lowercase, no digit, no symbol, contains whitespace. Empty list = acceptable. Please write the tests as well.
tasks.clean_requirements: A strong password like 'Correct-Horse7Battery' returns []. Each rule produces a specific, stable violation string; tests must assert the presence of specific violations and absence of others (e.g., 'alllowercase1!' flags only uppercase and length if applicable). Edge cases: empty string returns all applicable violations including too-short; exactly min_len chars is not too short; min_len-1 is; a password with an internal space is flagged; unicode letters like 'É' count as uppercase if str.isupper is used (tests must pin whichever behavior is chosen); symbol detection must not count letters/digits/whitespace.
tasks.failure_stakes: Weak passwords are accepted or strong ones are rejected with misleading messages, and the tests wouldn't catch either because they only check a list comes back.

tasks.title: IPv4 address and CIDR validator
tasks.user_request: Write `parse_cidr(s: str) -> tuple[str, int]` that validates an IPv4 address or CIDR block (e.g. `10.0.0.0/8`, or `192.168.1.5` meaning /32) and returns (normalized_ip, prefix_len). Raise ValueError for anything invalid. Don't use the ipaddress module—I want to see the logic. Tests please.
tasks.clean_requirements: Accepts four dot-separated octets 0-255 with optional /0-32 suffix; bare address returns prefix 32. Rejects: octet > 255 ('256.1.1.1'), fewer/more than 4 octets, empty octets ('1..2.3'), leading zeros ('01.2.3.4', must be pinned either way but tests must assert the chosen behavior), negative or non-numeric octets, prefix > 32, prefix < 0, '/' with empty prefix, whitespace, empty string. Tests must assert exact return tuples ('0.0.0.0', 0), ('255.255.255.255', 32), and use pytest.raises for each rejection class.
tasks.failure_stakes: Firewall or allowlist rules accept malformed network strings and either fail to apply or match more than intended.

tasks.title: CSV header validator
tasks.user_request: Before importing uploads I want `validate_headers(actual: list[str], expected: list[str], *, strict_order: bool = False) -> HeaderReport` where HeaderReport is a dataclass with `missing`, `extra`, `duplicates`, and an `ok` property. Header comparison should be case-insensitive and ignore surrounding whitespace. Write tests too.
tasks.clean_requirements: ok is True only when missing, extra, and duplicates are all empty (and order matches when strict_order=True). missing lists expected names not present; extra lists actual names not expected (reported in original casing); duplicates lists headers appearing more than once in actual (after normalization, e.g. 'Email' and ' email ' are duplicates). strict_order=True must flag an order mismatch even when sets are identical (tests must pin how: e.g. an `order_ok` field or ok=False). Tests must cover: exact match, case/whitespace variants matching, one missing + one extra, duplicate detection, empty actual list, and strict vs non-strict order.
tasks.failure_stakes: Uploaded files with misspelled or swapped columns are imported, loading data into the wrong fields.

tasks.title: URL validator with scheme and host allowlist
tasks.user_request: I need `validate_url(url: str, allowed_schemes=('https',), allowed_hosts=None) -> str` that returns the normalized URL (lowercased scheme and host, default port stripped) or raises `InvalidURL` with a reason. If allowed_hosts is given, the host must match exactly or be a subdomain of an entry. Use urllib.parse. Add pytest tests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Accepts 'https://Example.COM:443/path?q=1' and returns 'https://example.com/path?q=1'. Raises InvalidURL for: disallowed scheme (http when only https allowed), missing scheme ('example.com/x'), missing host ('https:///path'), host not in allowlist, userinfo in URL ('https://user:pw@example.com') — tests must pin whether rejected, and non-default port retained vs rejected (pin behavior). Subdomain matching: 'api.example.com' allowed by 'example.com' but 'notexample.com' is not (tests must check this prefix trap). Tests must assert exact normalized output strings and use pytest.raises(InvalidURL) with match on the reason text.
tasks.failure_stakes: An SSRF-style request to an unintended host passes validation because the host check does a naive substring match.

tasks.title: Business days between dates
tasks.user_request: I need a function `business_days_between(start: date, end: date, holidays: set[date] | None = None) -> int` that counts weekdays between two dates, excluding anything in the holidays set. Please implement it and give me a pytest file for it too.
tasks.clean_requirements: Implementation must count Mon–Fri days in the range (clearly document whether end is inclusive or exclusive, and tests must pin that down), skip weekend days, skip any date in holidays, and handle start > end (either return a negative count or raise ValueError — tests must assert whichever is chosen). Tests must cover: a plain Mon→Fri week (5 or 4 depending on inclusivity), a range spanning a weekend, start == end, a holiday falling on a weekday vs. a holiday falling on a weekend (which must not double-subtract), a multi-week span with a known hand-computed answer, and the start > end case. Tests must use concrete dates and assert exact integers, not just type or non-negativity.
tasks.failure_stakes: An off-by-one or weekend-holiday double-count silently corrupts SLA deadlines, payroll, and invoice due dates computed from this function.

tasks.title: Add N business days
tasks.user_request: Write `add_business_days(start: date, n: int) -> date` that moves forward n weekdays (skipping Saturday and Sunday), and negative n should move backward. Include pytest tests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Function must skip weekends in both directions; n == 0 returns start unchanged (even if start is a weekend — tests must assert the chosen behavior). Tests must assert exact result dates for: Friday + 1 → Monday; Monday − 1 → previous Friday; Wednesday + 5 → next Wednesday; a Saturday start with n=1 (define and assert whether it lands on Monday or Tuesday); n=0; a span of 20+ days crossing multiple weekends with a hand-verified date; and a large negative n. Tests must also check the result is never a Saturday/Sunday for n != 0 across a sample of inputs.
tasks.failure_stakes: Wrong landing dates push contractual deliverables and payment schedules onto weekends or the wrong week.

tasks.title: ISO 8601 duration parser
tasks.user_request: Can you implement `parse_iso_duration(s: str) -> timedelta` that handles strings like `PT1H30M`, `P2DT3H`, `P1W`, and `PT0.5S`? I don't need years/months support. Write pytest tests alongside it.
tasks.clean_requirements: Parser must handle days, weeks, hours, minutes, seconds (including fractional seconds), the `T` separator, and raise ValueError for malformed input (missing leading P, empty string, `P` alone, unknown designators like `P1Y`/`P1M`, time components without `T`, garbage text). Tests must assert exact timedelta values for: `PT1H30M` == timedelta(hours=1, minutes=30), `P2DT3H`, `P1W` == 7 days, `PT0.5S` == 500000 microseconds, `PT0S` == zero, `P1DT24H` == 2 days, and each invalid case must be asserted with pytest.raises(ValueError). Tests must not merely check isinstance(result, timedelta).
tasks.failure_stakes: Misparsed durations lead to retry backoffs, TTLs, or scheduled jobs firing at wildly wrong times.

tasks.title: Relative time formatter
tasks.user_request: I want a `humanize_delta(then: datetime, now: datetime) -> str` that returns things like 'just now', '5 minutes ago', 'in 3 hours', 'yesterday', '2 days ago', 'in 1 month'. Implement it and write pytest tests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Function must choose the largest applicable unit (seconds/minutes/hours/days/weeks/months/years), use singular vs. plural correctly ('1 minute ago' not '1 minutes ago'), prefix 'in' for future and suffix 'ago' for past, and return 'just now' for |delta| below some threshold. Tests must assert exact strings for: 0 seconds, 30 seconds, 1 minute, 59 minutes, 1 hour, 23 hours, 1 day (expect 'yesterday'/'tomorrow' if implemented), 6 days, 2 weeks, 1 month, 2 years, and at least two future cases. Tests must also cover a boundary exactly at a unit threshold (e.g., exactly 60 minutes → '1 hour ago') and a mixed timezone-aware pair of datetimes.
tasks.failure_stakes: Users see confusing or grammatically wrong timestamps like '1 days ago' or future events labeled as past in the UI.

tasks.title: Age in years from birthdate
tasks.user_request: Implement `age_in_years(birthdate: date, on: date) -> int` that returns someone's completed age on a given date. Watch out for Feb 29 birthdays. Add pytest tests please.
tasks.clean_requirements: Function must return completed years (not rounded), decrement by one if the birthday hasn't occurred yet this year, treat Feb 29 birthdays as occurring on Mar 1 (or Feb 28 — tests must pin down the chosen rule) in non-leap years, and raise ValueError if `on` is before birthdate. Tests must assert exact integers for: birthday exactly today, day before birthday, day after birthday, Feb 29 born person on Feb 28 and Mar 1 of a non-leap year, Feb 29 born person on Feb 29 of a leap year, a newborn (same date → 0), and the before-birth error case.
tasks.failure_stakes: Off-by-one ages break age-gated eligibility checks (legal age, insurance brackets, retirement) for people near a birthday.

tasks.title: Next weekday occurrence
tasks.user_request: Write `next_weekday(from_date: date, weekday: int, include_today: bool = False) -> date` where weekday is 0=Monday..6=Sunday, returning the next date that falls on that weekday. Please include a pytest test file.
tasks.clean_requirements: Function must return a date strictly after from_date unless include_today=True and from_date already matches, must always return a date within 7 days, and must raise ValueError for weekday outside 0–6. Tests must assert exact dates for: Monday→next Friday, Friday→next Monday (crosses weekend), same weekday with include_today=False (expect +7 days), same weekday with include_today=True (expect from_date), a transition across a month boundary, a transition across Dec 31→Jan, and pytest.raises(ValueError) for weekday=7 and weekday=-1. A parametrized test should verify result.weekday() == weekday for all 7 weekdays from a fixed date.
tasks.failure_stakes: A recurring report or meeting reminder lands a week late or on the wrong day without anyone noticing until the event is missed.

tasks.title: Round datetime to interval
tasks.user_request: I need `round_to_interval(dt: datetime, minutes: int, mode: str = 'nearest') -> datetime` that snaps a datetime to the nearest/floor/ceil multiple of N minutes within the hour (e.g. 10:07 → 10:05 for 5 minutes). Implement it with pytest tests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Function must zero out seconds and microseconds, support modes 'floor', 'ceil', 'nearest', define and test the tie-breaking rule for 'nearest' (e.g., 10:07:30 with 15-minute buckets), preserve tzinfo, and raise ValueError for minutes <= 0, minutes that don't divide 60 (or document support), or unknown mode. Tests must assert exact datetimes for: an already-aligned value in each mode (unchanged), floor and ceil across an hour boundary (10:58 ceil 15 → 11:00), ceil across midnight into the next day, nearest with the exact midpoint, a datetime with nonzero seconds/microseconds, a tz-aware input retaining its tzinfo, and pytest.raises for each invalid argument.
tasks.failure_stakes: Mis-bucketed timestamps skew time-series aggregations and billing periods, with ceil-across-midnight errors shifting data to the wrong day.

tasks.title: Add months with day clamping
tasks.user_request: Can you write `add_months(d: date, months: int) -> date` that adds calendar months but clamps the day to the last valid day of the target month (so Jan 31 + 1 → Feb 28, or Feb 29 in a leap year)? Negative months too. Pytest tests included please.
tasks.clean_requirements: Function must handle year rollover, negative months, and day clamping using the actual target month length (leap-year aware). Tests must assert exact dates for: Jan 31 2023 + 1 → Feb 28 2023; Jan 31 2024 + 1 → Feb 29 2024; Mar 31 + 1 → Apr 30; Dec 15 + 1 → Jan 15 next year; Jan 15 − 1 → Dec 15 previous year; +12 months → same day next year; +0 → unchanged; Feb 29 2024 + 12 → Feb 28 2025; Mar 31 − 1 → Feb 28/29; a large value like +25 months crossing multiple years. Tests should also verify that add_months(d, n) never produces an invalid date (no exception) across a range of month-end inputs.
tasks.failure_stakes: Subscription renewals and loan schedules starting on the 29th–31st crash or silently drift to the wrong day.

tasks.title: Interval overlap duration
tasks.user_request: Implement `overlap(a_start: datetime, a_end: datetime, b_start: datetime, b_end: datetime) -> timedelta` returning how long two time intervals overlap (zero if they don't). Also write pytest tests for it.
tasks.clean_requirements: Function must return max(0, min(ends) − max(starts)), raise ValueError if either interval has end < start, and treat intervals as half-open or closed consistently (tests must pin this: touching intervals where a_end == b_start should return timedelta(0)). Tests must assert exact timedeltas for: partial overlap, one interval fully containing the other (result equals the inner duration), identical intervals, disjoint intervals (zero), touching intervals (zero), argument order swapped giving the same result, zero-length interval inside another, mixed tz-aware intervals in different timezones representing the same instant, and pytest.raises(ValueError) for an inverted interval.
tasks.failure_stakes: Wrong overlap values miscalculate double-booking detection, on-call pay, and concurrent-usage billing.

tasks.title: Split range into daily chunks

tasks.clean_requirements: Days overdue = (as_of - due_date).days; due today or in the future is 'current'; 1-30, 31-60, 61-90 inclusive on both ends; 91+ is '90+'; invoices with zero balance are excluded; every bucket key is present with Decimal('0.00') even when empty; balances are summed as Decimal. Tests with as_of = 2024-06-30 must assert: due 2024-06-30 -> current; due 2024-06-29 -> 1-30; due 2024-05-31 (30 days) -> 1-30; due 2024-05-30 (31 days) -> 31-60; due 2024-04-01 (90 days) -> 61-90; due 2024-03-31 (91 days) -> 90+; a future due date -> current; a zero-balance invoice contributes nothing; empty input returns all five keys with 0.00; multiple invoices in one bucket are summed correctly.
tasks.failure_stakes: Misclassifying invoices at the 30/60/90-day boundaries sends collections notices to the wrong customers and misstates bad-debt reserves on the balance sheet.

tasks.title: Apply a payment across open invoices oldest-first
tasks.user_request: Write `allocate_payment(amount, invoices)` where invoices is a list of dicts with 'id', 'date', and 'balance'. Apply the payment to invoices oldest first, return the list of (id, amount_applied) and any leftover credit. pytest tests please.
tasks.clean_requirements: Sorts by date (not input order), skips zero-balance invoices, applies min(remaining, balance) to each, returns (allocations, unapplied_credit) as Decimals, raises ValueError for negative amount, and does not mutate the input list or dicts. Tests must assert: invoices INV1 100.00 (2024-01-05) and INV2 50.00 (2024-02-01) with payment 120.00 -> [('INV1', 100.00), ('INV2', 20.00)], credit 0.00; payment 200.00 -> both fully paid, credit 50.00; payment 0.00 -> [] and credit 0.00; input given in reverse date order still allocates to INV1 first; a zero-balance invoice receives no allocation entry; pytest.raises for a negative payment; after the call the original dicts still have their original balances.
tasks.failure_stakes: Allocating to the wrong invoice or mutating caller data causes customers to be dunned for invoices they already paid and corrupts the receivables ledger.

tasks.title: Parse money strings into Decimal
tasks.user_request: Our CSV imports have amounts like '$1,234.56', '-$5.00', '(5.00)' for negatives, and plain '1234'. Write `parse_money(s: str) -> Decimal` that normalizes these to a Decimal with two decimal places, and add a pytest test file.
tasks.clean_requirements: Strips whitespace, an optional leading '$', thousands separators, and treats both a leading '-' and parentheses as negative; always returns a Decimal quantized to 2 places; never goes through float; raises ValueError for empty strings, non-numeric input, more than two decimal places, and malformed grouping. Tests must assert: '$1,234.56' -> 1234.56; '1234' -> 1234.00; '-$5.00' -> -5.00; '(5.00)' -> -5.00; '  $0.50 ' -> 0.50; '0' -> 0.00; and pytest.raises(ValueError) for '', 'abc', '12.345', and '1,23.45'. At least one test must check result.as_tuple().exponent == -2 and that the return type is Decimal.
tasks.failure_stakes: A parser that accepts garbage or drops a negative sign imports wrong amounts into the books, and one that round-trips through float introduces cent errors on large totals.

tasks.title: Graduated tiered pricing
tasks.user_request: Implement `tiered_price(units, tiers)` for usage billing, where tiers is a list like `[(100, Decimal('0.10')), (500, Decimal('0.08')), (None, Decimal('0.05'))]` meaning the first 100 units cost 0.10 each, the next 400 cost 0.08, and everything above 500 costs 0.05. Write pytest tests for it as well.
tasks.clean_requirements: Graduated (not volume) pricing: each unit is charged at the rate of the tier it falls in; the upper bounds are cumulative and must be strictly ascending with only the last allowed to be None; returns a Decimal rounded to cents; negative units raise ValueError; non-ascending tier bounds raise ValueError; units beyond the last bound when the last bound is not None raise ValueError. Tests must assert: 0 -> 0.00; 50 -> 5.00; 100 -> 10.00; 101 -> 10.08; 500 -> 42.00; 600 -> 47.00; a single unbounded tier charges a flat rate; pytest.raises for negative units, for tiers [(500, ...), (100, ...), (None, ...)], and for 600 units against tiers ending at 500 with no None tier.
tasks.failure_stakes: Confusing graduated with volume pricing or mishandling the tier boundary bills heavy users at the wrong rate on every usage invoice.

tasks.title: Flatten nested JSON records for CSV export
tasks.user_request: I need to dump a list of nested JSON records into a CSV, so write me a `flatten_record(record, sep='.')` that turns nested dicts into a single-level dict with dotted keys (e.g. `{"a": {"b": 1}}` -> `{"a.b": 1}`). Lists should become indexed keys like `tags.0`, `tags.1`. Include pytest tests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Implementation must recursively flatten dicts, convert lists to indexed keys, leave scalars (including None, 0, '', False) untouched at their flattened path, and respect a custom separator. Tests must assert: a simple nested dict flattens correctly; multi-level nesting (3+ deep); lists produce `key.0`, `key.1` entries; an empty dict or empty list value either produces no key or a documented sentinel (and the test pins down which); falsy scalars like 0, '', False, None are preserved as values, not dropped; a flat record is returned unchanged; custom `sep='_'` is honored; top-level empty dict returns empty dict.
tasks.failure_stakes: If falsy values or empty containers are silently dropped, the exported CSV loses real data and nobody notices until a downstream report is wrong.

tasks.title: Type-coerce CSV string fields
tasks.user_request: Everything from csv.DictReader comes back as strings. Write `coerce_row(row: dict) -> dict` that converts values to int when they look like ints, float when they look like floats, True/False for 'true'/'false' (case-insensitive), None for empty strings, and leaves everything else as a str. Add pytest tests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Tests must assert exact types and values, not just truthiness: '42' -> 42 (int, not 42.0); '-7' -> -7; '3.14' -> 3.14; '1e3' -> 1000.0 float; 'TRUE'/'False' -> bool; '' -> None; 'abc' stays 'abc'; '007' or '0042' behavior is pinned down (leading zeros either stay str or become int, test asserts one); ' 42 ' with surrounding whitespace behavior is pinned; 'nan'/'inf' behavior is pinned (should probably remain strings); keys are preserved unchanged; an empty dict returns an empty dict; the original row is not mutated.
tasks.failure_stakes: Zip codes like '00501' silently becoming 501, or 'NaN' becoming float nan, corrupts the data for every row in the import.

tasks.title: Deduplicate records keeping newest
tasks.user_request: I get overlapping exports where the same customer appears multiple times with different `updated_at` ISO timestamps. Write `dedupe_latest(records, key='id', ts_field='updated_at')` that returns one record per key, keeping the one with the most recent timestamp, preserving first-seen order of keys. Please write pytest tests too.
tasks.clean_requirements: Tests must assert: duplicates collapse to exactly one record with the latest `updated_at`; output order follows the order in which each key was first encountered, not the order of the winning record; records with distinct keys are all retained; ISO timestamps that differ in date, hour, and seconds are compared chronologically (not lexically if formats differ — e.g. with/without 'Z' or offsets, or at minimum the test documents accepted format); a tie on timestamp keeps a deterministic record (test pins which: first or last); a record missing the ts_field either raises KeyError or is treated as oldest (test asserts the chosen behavior); a record missing the key field raises; empty input returns empty list; the input list is not mutated.
tasks.failure_stakes: Picking the wrong duplicate means stale customer addresses or balances overwrite correct ones in the destination system.

tasks.title: Left-join two lists of records
tasks.user_request: Write `left_join(left, right, on, prefix='right_')` that joins two lists of dicts on a shared key like SQL LEFT JOIN: every left record appears in the output, matching right-side fields are merged in (with the prefix applied to colliding column names other than the join key), and unmatched left rows get None for the right columns. Include pytest tests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Tests must assert: a matched row contains both sides' fields; an unmatched left row is present with None for every right-side column (and the test checks the actual column set, not just row count); a right-side field with the same name as a left field is prefixed and the left value is kept un-prefixed; the join key itself is not duplicated or prefixed; multiple right matches for one left key produce multiple output rows (one per match) — or the test pins down a documented alternative; right-only rows do not appear; empty left returns empty list; empty right returns left rows padded with None columns derived from... (test asserts behavior when right is empty, e.g. rows unchanged); inputs are not mutated.
tasks.failure_stakes: Dropping unmatched left rows or mis-handling name collisions silently loses or overwrites fields in the merged dataset.

tasks.title: Pivot long records to wide
tasks.user_request: I have long-format rows like `{'region': 'EU', 'metric': 'sales', 'value': 10}` and want them wide: one row per region with a column per metric. Write `pivot(records, index, column, value, fill=None)` returning a list of dicts, and write pytest tests for it.
tasks.clean_requirements: Tests must assert: two metrics for one region produce one row with both metric columns; a region missing a metric gets the `fill` value for that column (and the test checks a custom fill like 0 as well as the default None); the set of output columns is the union of all metric names across all rows, so every output row has identical keys; row order follows first appearance of each index value; duplicate (index, column) pairs are handled deterministically (last wins, or raise — test pins down which); a value of 0 or '' is not mistaken for missing and replaced by fill; empty input returns empty list; records missing the index/column/value field raise KeyError.
tasks.failure_stakes: Ragged rows or zeros being replaced by fill values produce a wide CSV that misaligns columns and misreports metrics.

tasks.title: Normalize CSV header names
tasks.user_request: CSV headers from clients are a mess: ' First Name', 'first-name', 'FIRST NAME', 'Total ($)'. Write `normalize_headers(headers: list[str]) -> list[str]` that converts each to snake_case ASCII identifiers (lowercase, non-alphanumerics collapsed to a single underscore, trimmed) and makes duplicates unique by appending `_2`, `_3`, etc. Add pytest tests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Tests must assert concrete outputs: ' First Name' -> 'first_name'; 'Total ($)' -> 'total' (trailing underscore stripped); 'first-name' and 'FIRST NAME' in the same list produce 'first_name' and 'first_name_2'; a third duplicate yields 'first_name_3'; a header that is empty or all-punctuation becomes a non-empty placeholder like 'column' (test pins down the name) and is deduped too; a header starting with a digit is handled (test pins down: prefixed or left as is); runs of multiple separators collapse to one underscore ('a  -  b' -> 'a_b'); output length equals input length; order is preserved; an empty list returns an empty list; already-clean headers pass through unchanged.
tasks.failure_stakes: Duplicate or empty normalized headers cause DictReader/DataFrame columns to overwrite each other, silently discarding entire columns of client data.

tasks.title: Group records and aggregate a field
tasks.user_request: Write `group_sum(records, by, field)` that groups a list of dicts by the `by` key and returns a dict mapping each group value to the sum of `field`, plus a count of rows per group — something like `{'EU': {'sum': 30, 'count': 2}}`. Values in `field` may be strings from a CSV, so parse them as numbers. Please include pytest tests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Tests must assert: two groups with multiple rows each sum and count correctly; numeric strings like '10' and '2.5' are parsed and summed (test checks the numeric result, e.g. 12.5, not a concatenated string '102.5'); a group with one row has count 1; a row whose `field` is empty/None is either skipped (count still increments or not — test pins down which) or raises; a non-numeric value like 'abc' raises ValueError; negative numbers reduce the sum; a `by` value of None or '' forms its own group rather than being dropped; empty input returns empty dict; records missing the `by` key raise KeyError; input list is not mutated.
tasks.failure_stakes: String concatenation instead of numeric addition or silently skipped rows produces totals that are plausibly wrong and hard to catch in a report.

tasks.title: Write heterogeneous records to CSV string
tasks.user_request: I have a list of dicts where not every record has the same keys. Write `records_to_csv(records, columns=None) -> str` that produces CSV text: if `columns` is given use exactly that order (missing values blank), otherwise use the union of keys in first-seen order. Values containing commas, quotes, or newlines need to come out quoted properly. Include pytest tests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Tests should round-trip the output through csv.DictReader and also check raw text where it matters. Must assert: header line equals the union of keys in first-seen order when columns is None; a record missing a key yields an empty field at that position (row length equals header length); explicit `columns` controls order and omits keys not listed; a value with a comma is quoted; a value with an embedded double quote is escaped as doubled quotes; a value with a newline is quoted and survives a round-trip; None is written as empty string; numbers like 0 are written as '0' not blank; empty records list with explicit columns yields just the header line; empty records with no columns yields empty string (or header-less — test pins down); line endings are consistent (test asserts '\n' or '\r\n' explicitly).
tasks.failure_stakes: A single unquoted comma or newline shifts every subsequent column in that row, corrupting the file for whoever imports it.

tasks.title: Validate records against a simple schema
tasks.user_request: Write `validate_records(records, schema)` where `schema` is a dict like `{'id': int, 'email': str, 'age': (int, None)}` (a tuple means optional/nullable). Return `(valid, invalid)` where invalid entries are `(index, record, [error messages])`. Also write the pytest tests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Tests must assert: a fully valid record lands in `valid` unchanged; a record with a wrong type for a required field lands in `invalid` with an error message naming the field (test checks the message contains the field name); a missing required field is an error; a missing optional field is fine; an optional field explicitly set to None is fine, but a required field set to None is an error; an unexpected extra key is either an error or ignored (test pins down which); a bool is NOT accepted where int is required (since bool subclasses int — test asserts `True` for an int field is rejected, or documents acceptance); a record with multiple problems reports all of them, not just the first; indexes in `invalid` match original positions; order of `valid` matches input order; empty input returns ([], []).
tasks.failure_stakes: Letting booleans or Nones through as ints means bad rows reach the database insert and fail halfway through a batch, or worse, succeed with garbage.

tasks.title: Diff two record sets by key
tasks.user_request: Write `diff_records(old, new, key='id')` that compares two lists of dicts and returns a dict with `added` (records only in new), `removed` (only in old), and `changed` (same key, different content) where each changed entry shows the key and a dict of `field: (old_value, new_value)` for the fields that differ. Add pytest tests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Tests must assert: a record present only in `new` appears in `added`; present only in `old` appears in `removed`; a record with the same key and identical content appears in none of the three; a record with one differing field appears in `changed` with exactly that field and the correct (old, new) tuple; a field present in new but absent in old shows up as (None/missing-sentinel, value) and vice versa (test pins down the sentinel); a change from 0 to None or '' to None is detected as a change (not treated as equal); multiple differing fields are all reported; the key field itself is not listed as changed; output order is deterministic (e.g. follows input order) and the test asserts it; duplicate keys within one input raise ValueError or are handled in a documented way; both inputs empty returns three empty collections; inputs are not mutated.
tasks.failure_stakes: A diff that misses falsy-value changes or mislabels added/removed rows feeds incorrect sync operations to a downstream system, deleting or skipping real updates.

tasks.title: Tag and push a release
tasks.user_request: Write a Python function `cut_release(version: str, repo_dir: str)` that creates an annotated git tag `v{version}` on the current HEAD and pushes it to origin. It should print the SHA that got tagged when it's done.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must run git via subprocess with check=True or explicitly inspect returncode for every command (rev-parse HEAD, tag -a, push origin tag). Should refuse to proceed if the working tree is dirty (`git status --porcelain` non-empty) or if the tag already exists (`git rev-parse --verify refs/tags/vX` succeeds). On tag-creation failure, must not attempt the push; on push failure, must raise/exit non-zero and ideally delete the local tag so the repo isn't left in a half-released state. Must not print a success message unless push actually returned 0. Tests should cover: tag already exists, dirty tree, push rejected (non-zero exit), happy path.
tasks.failure_stakes: A release that appears to succeed but was never pushed (or tagged the wrong commit) means CI deploys nothing or deploys the wrong code while the team believes v1.2.3 shipped.

tasks.title: Nightly pg_dump to gzipped file
tasks.user_request: I need a small script that dumps our Postgres database with `pg_dump`, gzips it to `/backups/db-YYYYMMDD.sql.gz`, and then deletes backup files older than 14 days. Connection info comes from the usual PG* env vars.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must check pg_dump's return code (and gzip's if piped as separate processes; a shell pipeline without `pipefail` hides pg_dump failure). Must write to a temp file and only rename to the final name after a successful dump, so a failed dump doesn't produce a zero-byte or truncated file that looks valid. Must skip the deletion of old backups entirely if today's dump failed. Should verify the output file is non-empty. Tests should cover: pg_dump exits non-zero (no final file created, old backups untouched, script exits non-zero), happy path produces file and prunes only files older than 14 days.
tasks.failure_stakes: A silently failing dump that still prunes old backups leaves the user with zero usable backups exactly when they need one.

tasks.title: Check out pinned commits for a build
tasks.user_request: Write `sync_deps(lockfile_path)` that reads a JSON file mapping `{name: {"url": ..., "sha": ...}}`, clones each repo into `deps/<name>` if it isn't there already, and checks out the exact SHA. Return a list of names that were updated.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must check return codes of git clone, git fetch, and git checkout for each dep. If a checkout fails (bad SHA, network error), must raise or return a clear failure rather than leaving the dep on whatever branch the clone landed on. Must verify after checkout that `git rev-parse HEAD` equals the requested SHA (prefix match acceptable). Should not add a name to the 'updated' list unless its checkout succeeded. Should handle an existing `deps/<name>` directory that is not a git repo. Tests: nonexistent SHA causes failure and is not reported as updated; already-at-SHA dep is skipped; clone failure doesn't abort processing in a way that misreports earlier successes.
tasks.failure_stakes: Building against the wrong dependency commit produces binaries that don't match the lockfile, leading to irreproducible builds and subtle production bugs.

tasks.title: Auto-commit generated docs
tasks.user_request: We regenerate API docs in CI and want to commit them back. Write a function `commit_generated(paths: list[str], message: str) -> bool` that stages the given paths, commits if there are changes, and pushes. Return True if a commit was pushed, False if there was nothing to commit.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must distinguish `git diff --cached --quiet` exit 1 (changes present) from exit 0 (none) from exit >=2 (error) — can't just treat non-zero as 'has changes'. Must check return codes of git add, commit, and push separately. Must not return True unless push succeeded; a push rejection (e.g. non-fast-forward) must surface as an exception or non-zero exit, not a False. Should ensure user.name/user.email are set or pass -c config so commit doesn't fail cryptically in CI. Tests: no changes returns False and no commit made; changes present leads to commit+push and True; push failure raises; git error (e.g. not a repo) raises rather than returning False.
tasks.failure_stakes: Treating a git error as 'no changes' means docs silently stop updating for weeks, or a failed push is reported as success and the CI job goes green with stale docs.

tasks.title: Deploy static site with rsync
tasks.user_request: Write a deploy script that builds the site with `npm run build`, then rsyncs `dist/` to `deploy@web01:/var/www/site/` with `--delete`. It should print how long each step took.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must check the return code of `npm run build` and abort before rsync if it fails (otherwise `--delete` syncs an empty or partial dist/ and wipes the live site). Must verify `dist/` exists and is non-empty before running rsync with --delete. Must check rsync's return code and exit non-zero on failure (rsync returns 23/24 for partial transfers — these must not be treated as success). Timing output must not imply success when a step failed. Tests: build failure → rsync never invoked, exit non-zero; empty dist → rsync not invoked; rsync exit 23 → script exits non-zero.
tasks.failure_stakes: A failed build followed by rsync --delete takes the production website offline by deleting every file on the server.

tasks.title: Batch transcode videos and remove originals
tasks.user_request: Can you write a script that walks a directory, converts every `.mov` to `.mp4` with ffmpeg (`-c:v libx264 -crf 23`), and deletes the original once converted? Should be resumable if I run it again.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must check ffmpeg's return code and only delete the .mov if ffmpeg exited 0 and the output .mp4 exists with non-zero size. Should write to a temporary output name and rename on success so an interrupted run doesn't leave a partial .mp4 that gets treated as 'already converted' on the next run. Resumability must be based on the presence of a complete .mp4, not a partial one. Should continue past a failed file but report failures and exit non-zero at the end if any failed. Tests: ffmpeg failure leaves original intact and no .mp4; partial output from prior run is redone; success deletes original.
tasks.failure_stakes: Deleting the source video after a failed or truncated transcode destroys the only copy of irreplaceable footage.

tasks.title: Build and push Docker image tagged with git SHA
tasks.user_request: Write `build_and_push(image: str)` that figures out the short git SHA of HEAD, runs `docker build -t {image}:{sha} .`, pushes it, and also tags/pushes `latest` if we're on the main branch. Return the full image reference that was pushed.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must check the return code of `git rev-parse` (not in a repo / detached edge cases) and of each docker build/tag/push call. Must not push `latest` if the SHA push failed. Should refuse to tag `latest` from a dirty working tree or when branch detection (`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`) fails. Must raise/exit non-zero on any failure rather than returning a reference that was never pushed. Tests: docker build non-zero → no push attempted; sha push fails → latest not tagged; on non-main branch → latest not pushed; return value only on full success.
tasks.failure_stakes: A `latest` tag pushed when the real build failed means every environment pulling `latest` deploys a stale or wrong image while the pipeline reports success.

tasks.title: Verify GPG signatures on downloaded artifacts
tasks.user_request: Write a function `verify_all(artifact_dir)` that, for every `*.tar.gz` with a matching `.asc` file, runs `gpg --verify` and returns a dict of filename → True/False. Files without a signature should also show up as False.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must use gpg's return code (0 = good signature) rather than parsing stdout, and must treat any non-zero exit (bad signature, missing key, gpg not installed, file unreadable) as False — never True. Must not let a FileNotFoundError for the gpg binary propagate as a crash that skips remaining files silently; should either raise clearly or mark all as False. Should pass explicit `--verify sig data` argument order so gpg doesn't verify the wrong file. Tests: valid signature → True; tampered tarball → False; missing .asc → False; gpg missing → raises or all False, not an unhandled traceback mid-loop that leaves results incomplete.
tasks.failure_stakes: Reporting an unverified or tampered artifact as verified lets a malicious or corrupted package into the install pipeline.

tasks.title: Run DB migration then restart service
tasks.user_request: Write a deploy step `migrate_and_restart()` that runs `alembic upgrade head` in the app directory and then `systemctl restart myapp`. Log the output of each command.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must check alembic's return code and NOT restart the service if the migration failed (otherwise the new code starts against an old schema). Must check systemctl's return code and exit non-zero if the restart failed. Should capture stdout/stderr and log them even on failure so the error is visible. Should optionally verify `systemctl is-active myapp` after restart. Tests: alembic non-zero → systemctl never called, exits non-zero; restart fails → exits non-zero; both succeed → exits 0 and both commands invoked in order.
tasks.failure_stakes: Restarting the app after a half-applied migration causes runtime errors or data corruption against a mismatched schema.

tasks.title: Create archive and upload with aws cli
tasks.user_request: I want a script that tars up `./exports/`, uploads the archive to `s3://acme-exports/` with the aws CLI, and then empties the exports directory so the next run starts fresh.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must check tar's return code (tar returns 1 for 'file changed while reading' and 2 for fatal errors — neither should be treated as success) and verify the archive is non-empty before uploading. Must check `aws s3 cp` return code and only delete the contents of `./exports/` if the upload succeeded. Should ideally confirm the upload with `aws s3 ls` or `head-object` before deletion. Must exit non-zero on any failure and leave local data in place. Tests: tar failure → no upload, no deletion; upload failure → no deletion, exit non-zero; happy path → directory emptied.
tasks.failure_stakes: Deleting the local exports after a failed upload permanently loses the data that was supposed to be archived.
