tasks.title: Fetch all pages of orders
tasks.user_request: Write a function fetch_all_orders(base_url, api_key) that pulls every order from GET /orders. The API returns {"results": [...], "next": "<url or null>"} and you follow next until it's null. Return a flat list of orders.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must call response.raise_for_status() (or check status_code) on every page, not just the first, and raise or surface a clear error rather than returning a partial list when a later page fails. Must handle a response body that isn't JSON or lacks the 'results' key by raising rather than silently returning []. Should use a timeout on requests.get. Should pass the API key on every page request (including when 'next' is a full URL). Tests should assert: all pages are concatenated; a 500 on page 2 raises and does not return page 1 alone; a missing 'results' key raises; 'next': null terminates.
tasks.failure_stakes: A downstream report or reconciliation silently runs on half the orders and nobody notices the missing revenue until an audit.

tasks.title: Upload files then remove local copies
tasks.user_request: I need a script that takes a directory of .log files, POSTs each one as multipart to https://ingest.example.com/upload with a bearer token, and deletes the local file once it's uploaded so the disk doesn't fill up. Print a summary at the end.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must only delete a local file after confirming the upload succeeded (2xx status, ideally also validating any success indicator in the response body if the request describes one). On non-2xx, requests exceptions (timeout, connection error), or an open() failure, the file must be left in place and the failure recorded. Must use a timeout. Summary must list uploaded vs failed files, and the script should exit non-zero if any upload failed. Tests should assert: file deleted after 200; file retained after 500 / 401 / ConnectionError; one failure does not stop processing of remaining files; exit code reflects failures.
tasks.failure_stakes: Log files get deleted after a rejected upload and the data is permanently lost.

tasks.title: Stream a large download to disk
tasks.user_request: Give me download_file(url, dest_path) that streams a big binary file with requests (iter_content) and saves it to dest_path. It's for pulling nightly database dumps so it needs to work for multi-GB files.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must check the status code before writing anything (a 404/500 HTML error page must not be written as the dump). Should write to a temporary file in the same directory and atomically rename to dest_path only on success, so an interrupted or failed download never leaves a truncated file at dest_path. If Content-Length is present, should compare bytes written against it and raise on mismatch. Must use a timeout and clean up the temp file on any exception. Tests should assert: successful stream produces correct bytes at dest_path; non-200 raises and dest_path does not exist; a ChunkedEncodingError/ConnectionError mid-stream leaves no (or no partial) dest_path; Content-Length mismatch raises.
tasks.failure_stakes: A truncated or HTML-error 'database dump' gets restored into production and the restore fails or loads garbage.

tasks.title: Bulk delete stale resources
tasks.user_request: Write delete_resources(base_url, ids, session) that sends DELETE /resources/{id} for each id in the list and returns which ones were deleted. There can be a few hundred ids.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must inspect each response's status code individually: treat 200/204 (and arguably 404 as already-gone, if documented) as success, treat 4xx/5xx and requests exceptions as failure for that id. Must not stop at the first failure and must not report an id as deleted when its request failed. Return value must distinguish succeeded ids from failed ids (with status/error), or raise with full detail at the end. Must use a timeout. Tests should assert: mixed 204/500/ConnectionError responses yield the correct partition; a 403 is not counted as deleted; all ids are attempted.
tasks.failure_stakes: The caller records resources as deleted that still exist (or vice versa), leading to billing errors or orphaned data that gets purged elsewhere based on the wrong list.

tasks.title: Poll an async export job
tasks.user_request: Write wait_for_export(client_base, job_id) that polls GET /exports/{job_id} every 2 seconds until the job's "status" is "complete" and then returns the "download_url" from the response. Add a max wait of 10 minutes.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must check the HTTP status on every poll and raise on persistent non-200 (not loop forever on a 404/500 or treat an error body as 'still running'). Must handle a terminal failure status (e.g. 'failed' / 'cancelled') by raising with the job's error details instead of polling until timeout. Must raise a clear timeout error when the max wait is exceeded rather than returning None. Must handle a missing 'status' or 'download_url' key by raising. Must use a request timeout and should allow sleep to be injected/patched for tests. Tests should assert: pending→complete returns URL; 'failed' status raises promptly; 500 responses raise; exceeding max wait raises TimeoutError; missing download_url raises.
tasks.failure_stakes: A nightly pipeline hangs for ten minutes on a failed job and then proceeds with download_url=None, crashing or producing an empty export.

tasks.title: Cache exchange rates to a JSON file
tasks.user_request: I want get_rates(cache_path) that fetches https://api.exchangerate.example/latest?base=USD, writes the JSON to cache_path, and returns the "rates" dict. If the fetch doesn't work, fall back to whatever's in the cache file.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must check status code and parse JSON before writing the cache, so a 429/500 or non-JSON body never overwrites a good cache. Must validate the payload has a 'rates' dict before caching. Should write the cache atomically (temp file + rename). Fallback must handle a missing or corrupt cache file by raising a clear error (not returning None or crashing with a bare JSONDecodeError). Must use a timeout. Tests should assert: successful fetch writes cache and returns rates; 500 with existing cache returns cached rates and leaves file unchanged; 500 with no cache raises; a 200 with malformed body does not clobber the cache.
tasks.failure_stakes: A rate-limit error page overwrites the only cached rates, and every subsequent pricing calculation fails or uses garbage until someone notices.

tasks.title: Bulk update emails from CSV
tasks.user_request: Write a script that reads users.csv (columns: user_id,new_email) and PATCHes each one to /api/users/{user_id} with {"email": new_email}. At the end write results.csv with a row per user saying whether it worked.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must check each PATCH's status code: 2xx is success; 404, 409, 422, 5xx, and requests exceptions are failures, each recorded with the status/error message in results.csv. Must continue past failures. Must handle a malformed CSV row (missing column, empty email) without aborting the whole run or sending a bad request. Must use a timeout. Should exit non-zero if any update failed. Tests should assert: results.csv reflects 200 vs 409 vs ConnectionError accurately; no row is marked ok on a 4xx; all rows are attempted; exit code is non-zero when failures exist.
tasks.failure_stakes: Support tells users their emails were updated based on a results file that marked rejected PATCHes as successful, and password resets go to dead addresses.

tasks.title: Create project then assign owner
tasks.user_request: Write create_project_with_owner(api, name, owner_id) that POSTs to /projects to create the project, then POSTs to /projects/{id}/members with {"user_id": owner_id, "role": "owner"}. Return the new project id.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must check the first POST's status and that the response contains an id before attempting the second call; a failed or id-less create must raise, not POST to /projects/None/members. Must check the second POST's status; if adding the owner fails, must not return the id as if fully successful — either roll back by DELETEing the project (and check that too) or raise an error that clearly includes the orphaned project id. Must use timeouts. Tests should assert: both 201s return the id; create 500 raises with no member call made; member call 403 results in rollback DELETE or a raised error naming the project id; missing 'id' in create response raises.
tasks.failure_stakes: Orphaned ownerless projects accumulate that nobody can access or delete, or the caller proceeds assuming the user has owner access and later writes fail.

tasks.title: OAuth client-credentials token helper
tasks.user_request: Write get_access_token(token_url, client_id, client_secret) that POSTs the client-credentials grant (form-encoded) and returns the access token string. We'll call it before each batch of API requests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must check the status code and raise with the error body (OAuth servers return 400/401 with {"error": ...}) rather than attempting to read the token from an error response. Must verify 'access_token' is present and non-empty in the JSON, raising otherwise; must handle a non-JSON body. Must use a timeout. Must not log or include the client_secret in exception messages. Tests should assert: 200 with token returns the string; 401 {"error":"invalid_client"} raises with that error visible; 200 without access_token raises; non-JSON 200 raises; secret does not appear in the raised message.
tasks.failure_stakes: The script returns None or an error string as the 'token', every subsequent request 401s with a confusing message, or the secret leaks into logs.

tasks.title: Multi-endpoint health check CLI
tasks.user_request: Make a small CLI healthcheck.py that takes a list of URLs, GETs each one, and prints a table of url / status / latency. Our deploy script will run it after each release.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must use a per-request timeout and catch requests exceptions (Timeout, ConnectionError, SSLError) per URL, reporting them as failures without crashing the whole run. Must treat non-2xx status codes as unhealthy, not just 'no exception'. Must exit with a non-zero code if any URL is unhealthy so the deploy script can act on it, and zero only when all pass. Should still check every URL even after one fails. Tests should assert: all 200s → exit 0; one 503 → exit non-zero and that row shows 503; a ConnectionError → non-zero with the error shown; a Timeout → non-zero; remaining URLs are still checked after a failure.
tasks.failure_stakes: The deploy script sees exit 0 from a health check that swallowed a timeout or a 503 and declares a broken release healthy.

tasks.title: Gzip rotated logs then remove originals
tasks.user_request: Write a function compress_rotated(log_dir) that finds files matching *.log.[0-9]+ in log_dir, compresses each one by shelling out to gzip, and removes the uncompressed original once it's compressed. Return the list of files it produced.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must run gzip via subprocess (e.g. subprocess.run(['gzip', '-k' or without -k, path])) and check the returncode (or use check=True and catch CalledProcessError) before deleting the original; on non-zero return the original must be left intact and the failure recorded/raised. Should skip files that already have a .gz counterpart or handle gzip's refusal to overwrite. FileNotFoundError for a missing gzip binary must surface clearly, not as a generic crash with originals half-processed. Tests should assert: original removed only when gzip succeeds; original preserved and error reported when gzip exits non-zero; returned list matches actual .gz files created.
tasks.failure_stakes: If the original is unlinked regardless of gzip's exit status, a failed or interrupted compression (disk full, bad binary) silently destroys the log file.

tasks.title: Numbered log rotation shift
tasks.user_request: I need a rotate(path, keep=5) helper that does classic numbered rotation: app.log.4 -> app.log.5, ... app.log -> app.log.1, dropping anything beyond keep. Just use os.rename.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must shift from highest index downward so nothing is overwritten prematurely, and each os.rename/os.remove must be checked: OSError (PermissionError, missing file mid-shift, cross-device) must be caught and reported with the file involved, not swallowed. If the base file does not exist it should be a no-op or explicit result, not a traceback. Files beyond keep must be removed with failures reported. Tests should assert correct final numbering with a full set, with gaps (e.g. app.log.2 missing), that the oldest is deleted when exceeding keep, and that a rename failure (e.g. read-only dir) raises/returns an error rather than silently leaving a partial shift.
tasks.failure_stakes: A sloppy shift order or an ignored rename error overwrites or orphans log generations, and the app keeps writing to a file that will never be rotated again.

tasks.title: Delete logs older than N days
tasks.user_request: Write purge_old_logs(directory, max_age_days) that removes every *.log and *.log.* file whose mtime is older than max_age_days and returns how many bytes were freed. It runs from cron nightly.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must stat each file and handle FileNotFoundError (file vanished between listing and stat/remove) and PermissionError/OSError on os.remove individually: continue with remaining files, but collect and report the failures (return them or raise at the end with a summary), never silently count a failed delete as freed bytes. Bytes freed must be computed from files actually removed. A non-existent or unreadable directory must produce a clear error, not an empty success. Tests should use tmp_path with os.utime to set old/new mtimes and assert: only old files removed, byte count matches removed files, a file made undeletable (or mocked os.remove raising) is reported and not counted.
tasks.failure_stakes: Reporting bytes as freed when removes failed means disks quietly fill up while the nightly job reports success.

tasks.title: Ship rotated logs to archive endpoint
tasks.user_request: Write ship_logs(log_dir, base_url) that PUTs each *.log.gz in log_dir to base_url/<filename> with requests and deletes the local copy after upload so the box doesn't fill up. Use a 60 second timeout.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must check the HTTP response status (response.ok / raise_for_status, treating 2xx as success) before deleting the local file; 4xx/5xx, timeouts, and ConnectionError must leave the local file in place and be reported per-file, continuing or aborting explicitly rather than crashing mid-batch unnoticed. Should open files in binary mode and close them. Return/report which files shipped and which failed. Tests should mock requests.put and assert: file deleted on 200/201; file kept on 500, on 403, and on a raised Timeout; summary lists failures.
tasks.failure_stakes: Deleting the local copy after a failed or rejected upload permanently loses audit logs with no record that anything went wrong.

tasks.title: Copy-truncate rotation for an open log
tasks.user_request: Our service keeps its log file open, so write copytruncate(src, dst) that copies src to dst and then truncates src to zero length, like logrotate's copytruncate option.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must only truncate src after the copy fully succeeded: catch OSError from the copy (disk full, permission), optionally verify dst size matches src size at copy time and flush/fsync dst, and if the copy fails leave src untouched and raise/return an error. If dst already exists, must not silently clobber it without that being the documented behavior. Truncate via opening src in r+ / os.truncate and handle OSError there too (reporting that a copy exists but truncation failed). Tests should assert: dst content equals original src and src is empty on success; when copy fails (mock shutil.copyfile or unwritable dst dir) src is unchanged and no partial dst is reported as success.
tasks.failure_stakes: Truncating after a failed copy throws away the only copy of the log data.

tasks.title: Batch-purge old rows from a SQLite log table
tasks.user_request: Write purge_log_rows(db_path, older_than_ts, batch_size=1000) that deletes rows from the `events` table with ts < older_than_ts in batches so we don't hold a giant lock, and returns the total rows deleted.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must loop DELETE ... WHERE rowid IN (SELECT rowid FROM events WHERE ts < ? LIMIT ?) committing each batch, using cursor.rowcount to count and to detect completion. sqlite3.OperationalError (database is locked, missing table) and other sqlite3.Error must be caught, the current transaction rolled back, and the error surfaced along with how many rows were already committed; must not report a count that includes a failed batch. Connection must be closed in all paths. Tests should assert: correct count with fewer and more rows than batch_size, rows newer than cutoff remain, missing table raises a clear error, and a mocked failure on the second batch leaves first batch committed and reports the error.
tasks.failure_stakes: An ignored OperationalError returns a bogus count and the table silently stops being purged until the DB fills the disk.

tasks.title: Wrapper around logrotate command
tasks.user_request: Write run_logrotate(config_path, force=False) that runs the system logrotate binary against the given config with --state in /var/lib/myapp/logrotate.state and returns its combined output. We call it from a Python scheduler.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must invoke subprocess.run with capture_output/text and check returncode: non-zero must raise (or return a result flagged as failed) including stderr, since logrotate exits non-zero on partial failures while still printing normal output. Must handle FileNotFoundError for a missing binary and a missing config file with clear messages. Should pass --force only when requested and a timeout to avoid hanging the scheduler, handling TimeoutExpired. Tests should mock subprocess.run and assert: args built correctly; returncode 1 with stderr raises/flags failure with stderr included; returncode 0 returns output; missing binary produces a clear error.
tasks.failure_stakes: Treating a non-zero logrotate exit as success means rotation silently stops working and the scheduler keeps reporting green while disks fill.

tasks.title: Free disk space by deleting oldest logs
tasks.user_request: Write free_space(log_dir, min_free_bytes) that, while free space on the partition holding log_dir is below min_free_bytes, deletes the oldest *.log.* file in that directory. Return a list of what it deleted.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must use shutil.disk_usage and re-check after each deletion; must handle the case where no deletable files remain (stop and report that the target was not reached rather than looping forever or crashing on an empty list). os.remove failures (PermissionError, FileNotFoundError) must be handled: skip that file, record the failure, and continue to the next oldest so one bad file doesn't abort or infinite-loop the job. OSError from disk_usage/listdir on a bad directory must surface. Tests should mock shutil.disk_usage to return a sequence of free values and assert: oldest-first order, stops once threshold met, stops with a 'could not reach target' signal when files run out, and a file that raises on remove is skipped and reported.
tasks.failure_stakes: An infinite loop or crash on one undeletable file leaves the partition full and the service unable to write anything.

tasks.title: Signal process to reopen logs after rotation
tasks.user_request: After we rotate nginx-style logs we need to tell the daemon to reopen them. Write reopen_logs(pidfile) that reads the PID from pidfile and sends SIGHUP, returning True on success.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must handle: pidfile missing or unreadable (FileNotFoundError/PermissionError), pidfile content not an integer, stale PID (ProcessLookupError from os.kill), and lack of permission to signal (PermissionError) — each should produce a distinct, reported failure (return False with reason or raise a specific exception), never a bare traceback or a silent True. Should refuse to signal PID <= 0. Tests should mock os.kill and use tmp_path pidfiles to assert: valid pid sends SIGHUP and returns True; missing file, garbage content, pid 0, ProcessLookupError, and PermissionError each yield a failure result identifying the cause.
tasks.failure_stakes: Reporting success when the signal never landed means the daemon keeps writing to the rotated/deleted inode and new logs are lost until restart.

tasks.title: Tar up a day's logs and remove them
tasks.user_request: Write archive_day(log_dir, date_str, archive_dir) that puts every file in log_dir starting with date_str into archive_dir/<date_str>.tar.gz and then removes the originals. Return the archive path.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must create the tarball with tarfile in a way that failures are detected: catch OSError/tarfile.TarError during add/close (disk full, unreadable source file), remove the partial archive on failure, and leave originals intact. Should write to a temp name and rename into place only after successful close, and should verify the archive (e.g. reopen and compare member names/count to the source list) before deleting originals. If no matching files exist, return/raise explicitly rather than producing an empty archive and claiming success. Deletion of originals must handle per-file OSError and report it. Tests should assert: archive contains all files, originals gone on success; mocked failure during add leaves originals and no archive; zero matches handled; a delete failure after a good archive is reported.
tasks.failure_stakes: Deleting originals after a partially written or corrupt tarball loses an entire day of logs irrecoverably.

tasks.title: Build, tag and push a Docker image
tasks.user_request: Write a script `release.py <image> <version>` that runs `docker build -t <image>:<version> .`, also tags it as `<image>:latest`, and pushes both tags to the registry. Print the final pushed tags at the end.
tasks.clean_requirements: Use subprocess.run for each docker command and check the return code of build, both tag/push steps (check=True or explicit returncode checks). If build fails, do not tag or push anything; if the version push fails, do not report success and do not push latest. Exit non-zero with the failing command's stderr on any failure; only print the 'pushed' summary when every step returned 0. Handle docker not being installed (FileNotFoundError) with a clear message.
tasks.failure_stakes: A failed build or push gets reported as a successful release, so the team deploys a stale or missing image and `latest` points at something that was never actually built.

tasks.title: Regenerate pip lockfile
tasks.user_request: I want a `freeze_lock.py` that runs `pip freeze` inside our venv (path passed as an argument) and writes the output to `requirements.lock` in the repo root, replacing whatever is there. It should also drop any `-e` editable lines.
tasks.clean_requirements: Run `<venv>/bin/pip freeze` (or Scripts/pip.exe on Windows) with subprocess, capture stdout, and check the return code; if it is non-zero or the venv pip does not exist, exit non-zero without touching requirements.lock. Write to a temp file in the same directory and os.replace it over requirements.lock so the existing lockfile is never left truncated or half-written. Filter out lines starting with `-e`. Refuse to write an empty lockfile (treat zero packages as an error).
tasks.failure_stakes: If pip fails, the script blanks or truncates the lockfile and the next CI run installs nothing (or the wrong set), silently producing a broken deployment.

tasks.title: Run make targets with per-target logs
tasks.user_request: Write `build.py` that runs `make clean`, `make build`, and `make test` in order, teeing each target's output into `logs/<target>.log`. At the end print a one-line summary like `clean OK, build OK, test OK` and the total time.
tasks.clean_requirements: Create the logs directory if missing. For each target run `make <target>` via subprocess, write combined stdout/stderr to logs/<target>.log, and check the return code. Stop at the first failing target (do not run `make test` if `make build` failed), mark it FAIL in the summary, and exit with that target's non-zero return code. Handle make not found / log file not writable with a clear error rather than a traceback. Summary must never say OK for a target that returned non-zero.
tasks.failure_stakes: Build or test failures get swallowed and the pipeline prints an all-OK summary, so broken artifacts move on to deployment.

tasks.title: Post-deploy health check with rollback
tasks.user_request: After we start a new container I want a script that polls `http://localhost:8080/health` until it returns 200, then marks the deploy good. If it isn't healthy within 60 seconds, stop the new container and start the previous one (names passed as args: `healthcheck.py <new_container> <old_container>`).
tasks.clean_requirements: Poll with requests.get using a timeout inside a loop that respects the 60s deadline; treat connection errors, timeouts, and any non-200 status as 'not yet healthy' (do not crash on ConnectionError). On success exit 0. On deadline exceeded, run `docker stop <new>` and `docker start <old>` via subprocess, check each return code, report if rollback itself failed, and exit non-zero in every unhealthy path. A 5xx or 404 response must not be treated as healthy.
tasks.failure_stakes: A broken deploy is declared healthy (or a failed rollback is reported as a rollback), leaving production serving errors with nobody alerted.

tasks.title: Bump version in VERSION file
tasks.user_request: Write `bump_version.py [major|minor|patch]` that reads the semver string from `VERSION`, increments the requested part, writes it back, and prints the old and new versions.
tasks.clean_requirements: Handle a missing VERSION file, a file that is not a valid `X.Y.Z` string, and an invalid part argument by printing an error and exiting non-zero without writing anything. Write the new version to a temp file in the same directory then os.replace it, so an I/O error (disk full, permission denied) cannot leave VERSION empty or corrupted; catch OSError on write and report it. Preserve a trailing newline convention and ensure patch bump of 1.2.9 gives 1.2.10 (numeric, not string, comparison).
tasks.failure_stakes: A malformed or half-written VERSION file poisons every downstream build with a bogus version, or the file is wiped entirely and the release pipeline breaks.

tasks.title: Download release artifact and verify checksum
tasks.user_request: Need a function `fetch_artifact(url, sha256, dest_path)` that downloads a wheel/tarball from our artifact server and saves it to dest_path, verifying the SHA-256 matches. We'll call it from the deploy script before `pip install`.
tasks.clean_requirements: Use requests.get(stream=True, timeout=...) and check response.status_code / raise_for_status so a 404 or 500 HTML error page is never saved as the artifact. Stream chunks to a temporary file while hashing; compare the digest to the expected sha256 (case-insensitive) and only os.replace into dest_path on match. On mismatch, HTTP error, or network exception, delete the temp file, leave any existing dest_path untouched, and raise a clear exception. Return the path on success.
tasks.failure_stakes: A corrupted, truncated, or tampered artifact (or an HTML error page) gets installed into production as if it were the real package.

tasks.title: Record deployment in SQLite ledger
tasks.user_request: We keep a `deploys.db` SQLite file with a `deployments(id, service, version, image_digest, deployed_at)` table. Write `record_deploy(db_path, service, version)` that runs `docker inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' <service>:<version>` to get the digest and inserts a row. `(service, version)` is unique.
tasks.clean_requirements: Run docker inspect via subprocess, check the return code and that stdout is a non-empty digest; if the image does not exist locally, raise/return an error and do not insert. Open the DB with a context manager / explicit commit; catch sqlite3.IntegrityError on the duplicate (service, version) and surface it as a meaningful error rather than a traceback, and catch sqlite3.OperationalError for missing table or locked DB. Do not commit a row with an empty or placeholder digest. Return the new row id on success.
tasks.failure_stakes: The deploy ledger ends up with rows pointing at non-existent images or missing rows entirely, so an incident rollback picks the wrong image or there is no record of what is running.

tasks.title: Prune old Docker images
tasks.user_request: Write a cleanup script that lists local images for a given repo (`docker images <repo> --format '{{.ID}} {{.Tag}} {{.CreatedAt}}'`), removes any created more than N days ago, and prints how many were removed.
tasks.clean_requirements: Check the return code of the `docker images` listing and parse each line defensively (skip <none> tags or malformed lines; parse the CreatedAt timestamp with a fallback). For each candidate run `docker rmi <id>` and check its return code individually: images in use by a running container will fail to remove, and that must be reported as skipped/failed rather than counted as removed. Continue past individual rmi failures, print removed vs failed counts, and exit non-zero if any removal failed. Never run rmi if the listing command itself failed.
tasks.failure_stakes: The script reports 'removed 12 images' when half failed, so disk keeps filling up and on-call believes cleanup is working until the host runs out of space.

tasks.title: Rolling restart across a host list
tasks.user_request: Write `rollout.py hosts.txt <image>` that, for every host in the file, runs `ssh <host> 'docker pull <image> && docker compose up -d'` one host at a time, and stops the rollout if more than 2 hosts have failed. Print a per-host status table at the end.
tasks.clean_requirements: Handle a missing or empty hosts file with a clear error. Run each ssh command with subprocess.run and a timeout; treat non-zero return codes and TimeoutExpired as failures for that host, capturing stderr for the report. Track failures, abort before starting the next host once failures exceed 2, and list remaining hosts as 'not attempted'. Exit non-zero if any host failed. A host must only be marked OK when the ssh command returned 0.
tasks.failure_stakes: A bad image gets pushed to the entire fleet because early failures were not noticed, or hosts that timed out are reported as updated when they are still running the old version.

tasks.title: Run migrations then restart service
tasks.user_request: Write a deploy step that runs `alembic upgrade head` from the app directory and then `systemctl restart myapp`, and finally checks `systemctl is-active myapp`. Log each step with a timestamp.
tasks.clean_requirements: Run alembic via subprocess with cwd set to the app dir and check its return code; if migrations fail, do not restart the service and exit non-zero with alembic's stderr. Check the return code of the restart command, then verify `systemctl is-active` returns 0 and prints `active`; if the service is not active after restart, exit non-zero and say so explicitly. Handle missing app directory / missing alembic binary with a clear message. The script must never print a 'deploy complete' line unless all three steps succeeded.
tasks.failure_stakes: The app gets restarted against a half-migrated schema (or stays down after a failed restart) while the deploy log claims success, causing an outage that nobody notices until users complain.

tasks.title: CSV to SQLite importer
tasks.user_request: Write a function `import_csv(db_path, csv_path, table)` that reads a CSV with a header row and inserts every row into the given table (columns match the header). It gets run nightly by cron on files that are a few hundred thousand rows, so make it reasonably fast. Return the number of rows inserted.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must wrap all inserts in a single transaction (executemany inside `with conn:` or explicit BEGIN/COMMIT) so a failure mid-file leaves the table unchanged rather than half-loaded. Must catch/propagate sqlite3.Error (e.g. IntegrityError on a bad row, OperationalError on missing table) and roll back rather than committing a partial load. Must handle a missing/unreadable CSV (FileNotFoundError/PermissionError) without touching the DB. Must close the connection on both success and failure. Return value must reflect actual inserted rows, not lines read. Tests should assert that a CSV with a bad row results in zero rows inserted and an exception/non-zero exit.
tasks.failure_stakes: A half-committed import leaves the nightly table with a random subset of rows, and downstream reports silently run on incomplete data.

tasks.title: Minimal migration runner
tasks.user_request: I keep numbered SQL files in `migrations/` like `001_create_users.sql`, `002_add_index.sql`. Write `run_migrations(db_path, migrations_dir)` that creates a `schema_migrations(version TEXT PRIMARY KEY, applied_at TEXT)` table if needed, applies any files not yet recorded in order, and records each one.
tasks.clean_requirements: Each migration must run inside its own transaction together with the INSERT into schema_migrations, so a migration that fails partway is rolled back and not recorded. Must stop at the first failing migration and raise/report which file failed with the sqlite3 error message, not continue to later files. Must use executescript or equivalent but ensure a failure inside executescript doesn't leave an implicit commit of earlier statements recorded as applied (check for autocommit behavior; explicitly BEGIN or verify). Must handle an unreadable SQL file without recording it. Must sort by filename numerically/lexically and skip already-applied versions. Tests should assert that after a broken migration 002, 001 is applied, 002 is not recorded, and 003 is not applied.
tasks.failure_stakes: A failed migration that gets recorded as applied means the schema is permanently out of sync with what the code expects, and the next deploy breaks in production.

tasks.title: Upsert with locked-database retry
tasks.user_request: Several worker processes write to the same SQLite file. Write `upsert_metric(db_path, name, value, ts)` that does an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(name, ts) DO UPDATE on a `metrics` table. We occasionally see 'database is locked' errors, so deal with that.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must set a busy timeout (`sqlite3.connect(..., timeout=...)` or PRAGMA busy_timeout) and additionally catch sqlite3.OperationalError whose message contains 'locked'/'busy' and retry a bounded number of times with a short backoff. Must re-raise (not swallow) after retries are exhausted so the caller knows the write was lost. Must not retry on other OperationalErrors (e.g. no such table) or IntegrityError—those should propagate immediately. Must commit the write and close the connection in a finally. Tests should assert the function raises after N failed attempts and that a non-lock error is raised without retrying.
tasks.failure_stakes: Silently dropping writes on lock contention produces gaps in metrics that nobody notices until they try to debug an incident from the missing data.

tasks.title: Promote staging rows to production table
tasks.user_request: We load data into `orders_staging` first, then need to move it into `orders`. Write `promote_staging(conn)` that copies all rows from `orders_staging` into `orders` and then empties the staging table. Return how many rows were moved.
tasks.clean_requirements: The INSERT INTO orders SELECT ... and DELETE FROM orders_staging must happen in one transaction so a failure (e.g. UNIQUE violation on orders) rolls back and staging is left intact. Must verify the number of rows inserted (cursor.rowcount) matches the staging row count before deleting, and raise if they differ. Must catch sqlite3.IntegrityError/sqlite3.Error, roll back, and re-raise or return a clear failure rather than swallowing it. Must not commit if the delete fails. Tests should assert that a duplicate key in staging results in no change to either table and an exception.
tasks.failure_stakes: If the insert fails but the delete still commits, the staged orders are gone forever with nothing in the production table to show for them.

tasks.title: SQLite backup with rotation
tasks.user_request: Write a script `backup_db.py <db_path> <backup_dir>` that creates a timestamped copy of a live SQLite database in `backup_dir` and then deletes backups older than the newest 7. The database is being written to by a running app while this executes.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must use the sqlite3 online backup API (`src.backup(dest)`) rather than shutil.copy of a live file. Must verify the new backup (e.g. open it and run `PRAGMA integrity_check` expecting 'ok', or at least a trivial query) before deleting any old backups. Must handle disk full / permission errors (OSError, sqlite3.OperationalError) during backup by removing the partial backup file and exiting non-zero without rotating. Must only count files matching the backup naming pattern for rotation. Must exit with a non-zero status and a message on any failure so cron alerts. Tests should assert that a failed backup leaves the existing backups untouched.
tasks.failure_stakes: A truncated or corrupt backup that still triggers rotation means the last good backups are deleted and there is nothing to restore from.

tasks.title: Incremental log ingester with offset tracking
tasks.user_request: Write `ingest_log(db_path, log_path)` that reads new lines from an append-only log file since the last run, parses each line as `timestamp level message` and inserts them into an `events` table. Keep track of the byte offset of where you left off in a `meta` table so repeated runs don't re-insert.
tasks.clean_requirements: The offset update in `meta` and the event inserts must be in the same transaction so a failure during insert does not advance the offset (which would permanently skip lines) and a crash after insert but before offset update does not double-insert on rerun. Must handle the log file being missing or truncated/rotated (offset > file size → reset to 0 or raise, not silently read nothing). Must handle unparseable lines deliberately (skip with a count, or fail the batch—either is fine but must be explicit, not an uncaught ValueError that leaves the transaction open). Must roll back on sqlite3.Error and propagate. Tests should assert that if the insert fails, the stored offset is unchanged.
tasks.failure_stakes: Advancing the offset after a failed insert permanently loses a chunk of log events; not advancing it atomically causes duplicate events on every retry.

tasks.title: Retention cleanup with VACUUM
tasks.user_request: Write `purge_old_sessions(db_path, days)` that deletes rows from `sessions` whose `last_seen` is older than N days, then runs VACUUM to reclaim space. Print how many rows were deleted and the file size before/after.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must commit the DELETE before VACUUM (VACUUM cannot run inside a transaction) and handle the sqlite3.OperationalError that occurs if attempted inside one. Must report the actual deleted count from cursor.rowcount, not an estimate. Must catch and report VACUUM failures (disk full, database locked) as a non-zero exit while making clear the DELETE already committed. Must use parameterized dates (compute the cutoff in Python, pass as parameter) rather than string formatting. Must handle a nonexistent DB file/table as an error rather than creating an empty database and reporting 0 deleted. Tests should assert that `days` is applied correctly at the boundary and that the function fails loudly when the table doesn't exist.
tasks.failure_stakes: Opening a wrong path creates a fresh empty database and reports '0 deleted, success', so the real sessions table grows unbounded while the cleanup job looks healthy.

tasks.title: Transfer credits between accounts
tasks.user_request: Write `transfer(conn, from_id, to_id, amount)` for an `accounts(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, balance INTEGER)` table that debits one account and credits another. Accounts can't go negative.
tasks.clean_requirements: Both UPDATEs must be in a single transaction with rollback on any failure. Must verify each UPDATE affected exactly one row (cursor.rowcount == 1) and roll back + raise if an account id doesn't exist. Must enforce the non-negative constraint either via a `WHERE balance >= ?` on the debit and checking rowcount, or via a CHECK constraint whose IntegrityError is caught and rolled back—either way the credit must not commit when the debit fails. Must reject non-positive amounts and from_id == to_id. Must use `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` or equivalent to avoid a read-then-write race between concurrent writers. Tests should assert insufficient funds leaves both balances unchanged and that a missing destination account rolls back the debit.
tasks.failure_stakes: A debit that commits while the credit fails makes money vanish from the system with no record of where it went.

tasks.title: Scrape API into SQLite
tasks.user_request: Write a script that fetches `https://api.example.com/items?page=N` for pages 1..P with `requests`, and stores each item's `id`, `name`, and `updated_at` into an `items` table in `items.db`, replacing existing rows by id. Pass P as a command-line argument.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must check the HTTP response status (`raise_for_status()` or explicit status check) and not insert anything from a non-2xx response or a body that fails to parse as JSON (requests.exceptions.RequestException, ValueError/JSONDecodeError). Must handle timeouts (pass a timeout to requests.get). Must insert each page's items in a transaction and commit per page or at the end, rolling back on sqlite3.Error so a bad item doesn't leave a partial page. Must decide and make explicit what happens on a failed page: stop with non-zero exit, or skip and report—but never silently continue counting it as success. Must validate that expected keys exist in each item before insert (KeyError handled). Exit non-zero if any page failed. Tests should assert that a 500 on page 2 does not corrupt page 1's committed data and results in a non-zero exit.
tasks.failure_stakes: Treating a 500 or an HTML error page as data (or skipping it silently) leaves the local table stale or garbage while the job reports success.

tasks.title: Archive table to CSV and truncate
tasks.user_request: Write `archive_and_clear(db_path, table, out_csv)` that exports every row of a table to a CSV file (with header) and then deletes all rows from the table, so we can ship the CSV off to cold storage. Return the number of rows archived.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must fully write and flush/close the CSV (ideally os.fsync) and confirm the row count written matches the table count before executing the DELETE. Must not delete if writing the CSV raises OSError (disk full, permission denied); in that case remove the partial CSV or leave it clearly marked and raise. Must write the CSV to a temp file and rename into place, or otherwise avoid leaving a truncated `out_csv` that looks complete. Must run the DELETE in a transaction and commit only on success; roll back and raise on sqlite3.Error. Must refuse to overwrite an existing out_csv silently (or make overwrite explicit). Tests should assert that a write failure leaves the table untouched and that a successful run yields CSV row count == original table count.
tasks.failure_stakes: Deleting the rows after a truncated CSV write destroys the only copy of the archived data.

tasks.title: Nightly tar backup with rotation
tasks.user_request: Write a Python script with a function backup_dir(src, dest_dir, keep_days) that creates a dated tar.gz of src in dest_dir using the tar command, then deletes any backups in dest_dir older than keep_days. I'll run it from cron.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must invoke tar via subprocess without shell injection (list args, no shell=True with interpolated paths) and inspect the return code (check=True or explicit returncode test). On nonzero return code or OSError (tar missing, dest unwritable, ENOSPC) it must remove the partial archive, skip the deletion/rotation step entirely, and exit nonzero / raise so cron reports failure. Should write to a temp name and rename only on success. Rotation must only match the script's own backup filename pattern and report (not silently swallow) unlink errors. Tests/examples should cover: tar failure leaves old backups intact and no zero-byte archive remains.
tasks.failure_stakes: A failing tar quietly produces an empty or partial archive while the rotation step purges the last good backups, leaving the user with no restorable copy.

tasks.title: rsync mirror with last-good-sync state file
tasks.user_request: Need a function mirror(src, dest) that mirrors /srv/data to backup@nas:/backups/data with rsync -a --delete and returns True on success. It should also write the time of the last good sync to /var/lib/backup/last_sync so Nagios can alert if it goes stale.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must run rsync as an argument list and check the return code. Only exit code 0 counts as success; codes like 23 (partial transfer), 24 (vanished files), 12 (protocol error), 255 (ssh failure) must result in False with stderr logged. The state file must only be updated when rsync returned 0, and should be written atomically (temp + os.replace). Must handle FileNotFoundError if rsync is not installed and OSError writing the state file. Should set a timeout or at least not hang forever without indication.
tasks.failure_stakes: A partial or failed rsync gets recorded as a good sync, monitoring stays green, and the user discovers months later that the mirror has been stale or incomplete.

tasks.title: Archive old logs and delete originals
tasks.user_request: Write archive_logs(log_dir, archive_dir) that tars up all *.log files older than 7 days in log_dir into a single timestamped tar.gz in archive_dir and then removes the originals to free up disk.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must only delete originals after the archive has been successfully written and closed, and after verifying it: re-open the archive (tarfile.open) and confirm each expected member is present with matching size, or at minimum confirm the archive opens and lists without error. If tarfile raises (OSError/ENOSPC, PermissionError) during creation, the partial archive must be deleted and no originals removed. Files that fail to be added must not be deleted. Per-file unlink errors must be reported, not swallowed. If no files qualify, do not create an empty archive. Tests should cover: write failure leaves originals intact; archive contents verified before deletion.
tasks.failure_stakes: A truncated archive from a full disk gets 'archived' and the original logs are deleted, permanently losing audit/log data that is often needed exactly during incidents.

tasks.title: Restore from tar.gz backup
tasks.user_request: Can you write restore_backup(archive_path, target_dir, force=False) that extracts a .tar.gz backup into target_dir? It should refuse to clobber an existing non-empty target_dir unless force=True.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must handle a missing archive (FileNotFoundError) and corrupt/truncated archives (tarfile.ReadError, EOFError, gzip.BadGzipFile) with a clear error rather than a traceback or a half-extracted tree. Must reject members with absolute paths or '..' components (or use filter='data' on 3.12+). Extraction should go into a temporary sibling directory and be renamed/moved into place only on complete success, or the partial target must be cleaned up on failure. OSError during extraction (ENOSPC, EACCES) must be surfaced with the member name. Return value / exception must distinguish 'refused: target not empty' from 'extraction failed'.
tasks.failure_stakes: A corrupt archive or full disk leaves a half-restored directory that looks like a successful restore, and the operator brings a service back up on top of incomplete data.

tasks.title: Upload backup archive via HTTP and delete local copy
tasks.user_request: Write upload_backup(path, url, token) that PUTs a backup archive to our storage API with a bearer token and then deletes the local file once it's uploaded. Use requests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must stream the file (not read into memory), set a timeout, and check the response status: only delete the local file on a 2xx response (ideally after confirming the server-reported size/ETag matches the local file). 4xx must raise/return failure without retry and without deleting; 5xx/429 and requests.ConnectionError/Timeout may be retried a bounded number of times, then fail. FileNotFoundError on the local path must be reported. The function must never delete the local file on any failure path, and must return or raise something the caller can act on.
tasks.failure_stakes: A 500 or dropped connection gets treated as success and the only copy of the backup is deleted locally while nothing exists on the server.

tasks.title: SHA-256 sidecar write and verify
tasks.user_request: Add write_checksum(archive) that writes archive.sha256 next to the file in sha256sum format, and verify_checksum(archive) that returns whether the file matches. We'll run verify before every restore.
tasks.clean_requirements: Hash must be computed in chunks. verify_checksum must return False (or raise a specific error) when the sidecar is missing, malformed, or the digest does not match — it must never return True in any error path. OSError reading either file must not be swallowed into a True result. write_checksum should write the sidecar atomically and fail loudly if the archive cannot be read. Tests should cover: matching file, modified/truncated archive, missing sidecar, garbage sidecar.
tasks.failure_stakes: A verify function that returns True when the sidecar is missing or unreadable lets a corrupted backup pass pre-restore checks and the corruption is discovered mid-restore.

tasks.title: pg_dump to gzip backup script
tasks.user_request: Write a script that runs pg_dump for a given database name, gzips the output to /backups/<db>-<date>.sql.gz, and prints the final path. A shell pipeline is fine if that's easiest.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must detect pg_dump failure despite the pipe: either use Popen for both processes and check both return codes (pg_dump's exit status is normally masked by gzip's), or use bash with 'set -o pipefail', or pipe pg_dump stdout directly into gzip.open in Python and check pg_dump.returncode after wait(). Must not interpolate the db name into a shell string. On failure, capture/print stderr, remove the partial .sql.gz, and exit nonzero. Should sanity-check that the result is non-empty (an empty dump from a failed auth is not a backup). Write to a temp name and rename on success.
tasks.failure_stakes: pg_dump fails (bad credentials, DB down) but gzip exits 0, so cron sees success and the backup directory fills with empty .sql.gz files that are useless when the database needs restoring.

tasks.title: SQLite backup manifest
tasks.user_request: We track backups in backups.sqlite with a table backups(id, path UNIQUE, size, sha256, created_at). Write record_backup(conn, path) that hashes the file and inserts a row, and latest_backup(conn) that returns the most recent row as a dict.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must use parameterized queries. record_backup must stat/hash the real file and surface FileNotFoundError/OSError rather than inserting a row for a nonexistent file. The insert must be in a transaction that is committed on success and rolled back on sqlite3.Error; sqlite3.IntegrityError on a duplicate path must be reported distinctly, not swallowed. latest_backup must return None (not raise IndexError) when the table is empty and must order by created_at or id, not rely on insertion order. Tests should cover duplicate path, missing file, empty table.
tasks.failure_stakes: The manifest ends up claiming backups exist that were never written or whose rows were never committed, so restore tooling points at files that don't exist.

tasks.title: Incremental backup with tar snapshot file
tasks.user_request: Write incremental_backup(src, dest_dir, snapshot_file) that uses GNU tar --listed-incremental to produce incremental archives. If snapshot_file doesn't exist yet it should just do a full backup.
tasks.clean_requirements: Because tar updates the snapshot file in place even when it later fails, the function must run tar against a copy of the snapshot file and only replace the real snapshot (os.replace) when tar exits 0. Must check the return code: 0 success; 1 (some files changed while being read) must at least be flagged/returned as a warning rather than silently treated as success; 2 or other must be failure with stderr reported. On failure the partial archive must be removed and the original snapshot left untouched. No shell=True with interpolated paths.
tasks.failure_stakes: A failed tar run still advances the snapshot file, so the next incremental believes those files were already backed up and they are silently excluded from every future archive.

tasks.title: rsync --link-dest snapshot with 'latest' symlink
tasks.user_request: Write snapshot(src, backup_root) that makes a Time-Machine style backup: rsync src into backup_root/<timestamp> using --link-dest=backup_root/latest, then repoint the latest symlink to the new snapshot.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must check the rsync return code and only move the 'latest' symlink when it is 0. The new snapshot should be created under a temporary/in-progress name (e.g. <timestamp>.partial) and renamed to its final name on success; on failure it must be removed or left clearly marked so it is never used as a future --link-dest. The symlink update must be atomic (create temp symlink, os.replace) and relative or absolute consistently. On first run, when 'latest' does not exist, omit --link-dest rather than passing a dangling path. Must handle FileNotFoundError for rsync and OSError creating directories, and report rsync stderr.
tasks.failure_stakes: A failed rsync leaves a half-populated snapshot that becomes 'latest', so every subsequent snapshot hardlinks against incomplete data and the user has a chain of backups that all share the same gaps.

domain: config file migration and atomic writes

tasks.title: Atomic JSON config save
tasks.user_request: Write a `save_config(path, data)` function that writes a dict to a JSON file so that a crash halfway through never leaves a half-written config. Should work on both Linux and macOS.
tasks.clean_requirements: Serialize to a temp file in the same directory as the target (tempfile.mkstemp or NamedTemporaryFile with dir=dirname), write, flush, os.fsync the file descriptor, then os.replace onto the target. If json.dumps, write, fsync, or replace raises, the temp file must be removed and the exception propagated (not swallowed); the original file must remain untouched. Optionally fsync the directory after rename. Tests should assert that a write failure leaves the original content intact and no stray temp file behind.
tasks.failure_stakes: A truncated or half-written config.json means the app fails to start or silently loads wrong settings after a crash or disk-full event.

tasks.title: INI to JSON bulk converter
tasks.user_request: I have a directory full of legacy `.ini` config files and want to convert each one to `.json` with the same base name, then remove the `.ini`. Can you write a script that does this for every file in a given folder?
tasks.clean_requirements: For each .ini file, parse with configparser and catch configparser.Error (and UnicodeDecodeError) per-file; a bad file must be reported and skipped, not crash the whole run or delete the source. Only delete the .ini after the .json has been fully written (ideally atomically). If writing the .json fails (OSError), the .ini must be kept. Script should report counts of converted/skipped/failed and exit non-zero if any failed. Tests should cover a malformed .ini being left in place.
tasks.failure_stakes: A parse or write failure in the middle of the loop deletes the only copy of a config while leaving no JSON behind, losing settings permanently.

tasks.title: Versioned config schema migration
tasks.user_request: Our config.json has a `schema_version` field and we're now at version 3. Write `migrate_config(path)` that applies the v1->v2 and v2->v3 migration functions as needed and writes the result back. v1->v2 renames `db_host` to `database.host`; v2->v3 converts `timeout` from seconds (int) to a string like `"30s"`.
tasks.clean_requirements: Read and json.load the file, surfacing JSONDecodeError/FileNotFoundError rather than defaulting to an empty dict. If schema_version is missing or greater than 3 or not an int, raise/refuse rather than guessing. Apply only the required steps in order, handle missing keys in the migration functions (e.g. no `timeout` key) without KeyError corruption, set schema_version to 3, and write back atomically (temp + os.replace) and/or after making a .bak copy. If already at v3, do nothing. Tests should assert v1 input ends at v3 with both transformations, and that an unknown version does not modify the file.
tasks.failure_stakes: A half-applied migration or a guessed version leaves the config in a state no version of the app can read, and the original is gone.

tasks.title: Update a key in a .env file
tasks.user_request: Write `set_env_var(path, key, value)` that updates (or appends) a `KEY=value` line in a `.env` file while keeping all other lines and comments exactly as they are.
tasks.clean_requirements: Read the file (treat missing file as empty only if explicitly intended, otherwise raise); replace the first matching `KEY=` line, append if absent; preserve other lines verbatim including comments and blank lines; write back via temp file in same directory + os.replace so a crash can't truncate the file; preserve original file mode (shutil.copymode/os.chmod) since .env files are often 0600. Propagate PermissionError/OSError instead of silently returning. Tests: existing key replaced, new key appended, comments untouched, permissions preserved.
tasks.failure_stakes: A truncated or world-readable .env either breaks every service that sources it or leaks secrets.

tasks.title: Merge user overrides into defaults
tasks.user_request: Write a function `load_effective_config(defaults_path, user_path)` that deep-merges the user's JSON config over the defaults and returns the merged dict. Also give it an option to write the merged result back to `user_path`.
tasks.clean_requirements: defaults file missing or invalid must raise (it's a program bug). If the user file is missing, use defaults; but if the user file exists and contains invalid JSON, raise JSONDecodeError rather than silently treating it as empty and (when write-back is enabled) overwriting the user's edits with defaults. Deep merge must recurse into nested dicts and let user values replace lists/scalars. Write-back must be atomic (temp + os.replace). Tests should assert that a corrupt user file is NOT overwritten.
tasks.failure_stakes: A single typo in the user's config gets 'fixed' by clobbering the whole file with defaults, destroying all their customizations.

tasks.title: Backup then write config
tasks.user_request: Before we overwrite `settings.yaml` with new content, I want to keep a timestamped backup like `settings.yaml.20240115T103000.bak` and prune to the 5 most recent. Write `write_with_backup(path, content, keep=5)`.
tasks.clean_requirements: Create the backup with shutil.copy2 and only proceed to write if the copy succeeded (if the source doesn't exist, skip backup deliberately, not via a bare except). Write the new content atomically (temp + os.replace). Prune only after a successful write; pruning must sort backups by name/mtime, remove the oldest, and tolerate/report OSError on individual deletions without aborting. Return the backup path (or None). Tests: backup exists with original content after write, newest 5 retained, failed write leaves original and backup intact.
tasks.failure_stakes: If the backup silently fails and the write then corrupts the file, there is no recovery point for the production settings.

tasks.title: Relocate config to XDG path
tasks.user_request: We're moving from `~/.myapprc` (INI) to `~/.config/myapp/config.toml`. Write a `migrate_legacy_config()` that converts the old file to TOML at the new location and removes the old one, so users with the old file get migrated on first run.
tasks.clean_requirements: If the new config already exists, do not overwrite it (leave both, or return a status indicating skipped). If the old file doesn't exist, return without error. Parse with configparser and surface parse errors rather than writing an empty TOML. Create the destination directory with os.makedirs(exist_ok=True). Write TOML (hand-emit or tomli_w) atomically via temp + os.replace, and only os.remove the legacy file after the new file is fully written; if writing fails, the legacy file must remain. Return an enum/status (migrated/skipped/none). Tests should cover 'destination already exists' and 'write fails keeps old file'.
tasks.failure_stakes: Users lose their entire configuration on upgrade because the old file was deleted before the new one was durably written, or their new config gets clobbered by stale legacy values.

tasks.title: Validate nginx config before swap
tasks.user_request: Write a deploy helper `install_nginx_conf(new_conf_text)` that writes the new config to `/etc/nginx/nginx.conf`, runs `nginx -t`, and reloads nginx with `systemctl reload nginx`. If the new config is bad it should roll back to the previous one.
tasks.clean_requirements: Save the current config (copy to .bak) before touching anything; write new content atomically. Run `nginx -t` via subprocess.run with capture_output and check returncode explicitly (no shell=True, no ignoring the result); on non-zero, restore the backup via os.replace and raise/return failure including stderr. Only then run `systemctl reload nginx` and check its returncode too; if reload fails, restore the backup and attempt reload again, reporting the failure. Handle FileNotFoundError if nginx/systemctl binaries are absent. Tests (mocking subprocess.run) should assert rollback happens when `nginx -t` returns 1 and that reload is never called in that case.
tasks.failure_stakes: Reloading with an unvalidated config, or ignoring a failed reload, takes down every site on the server and leaves a broken file in place.

tasks.title: Push config to fleet via HTTP
tasks.user_request: Write `push_config(hosts, config_dict)` that PUTs the JSON config to `http://{host}:8080/api/config` on each host and returns which hosts were updated. Use requests.
tasks.clean_requirements: Use a timeout on every request. For each host, treat non-2xx status (check response.ok or raise_for_status) and requests.RequestException (timeout, connection refused) as a failure for that host, continuing with the others. Return a structured result separating succeeded and failed hosts with reason/status code; do not return success if any host failed silently. Optionally send Content-Type header explicitly. Tests should mock requests.put returning 500 for one host and raising ConnectionError for another, asserting both appear in the failed list and the third in succeeded.
tasks.failure_stakes: A host that 500s or times out gets reported as updated, leaving the fleet running inconsistent configs that nobody knows about.

tasks.title: Locked concurrent config update
tasks.user_request: Multiple worker processes need to update counters in a shared `state.json` file. Write `update_state(path, mutator)` where `mutator` is a function that takes the current dict and returns the new one, and make it safe for concurrent callers.
tasks.clean_requirements: Acquire an exclusive lock (fcntl.flock on a dedicated lock file or the target, opened with os.O_CREAT) before reading; hold it through the write; release in a finally block. Treat a missing state file as {} only if intended, but a corrupt file (JSONDecodeError) must raise instead of resetting state to {}. Write via temp in same dir + fsync + os.replace while still holding the lock. If the mutator raises, the file must not be modified. Tests: two sequential updates both persist; corrupt file raises; mutator exception leaves file unchanged.
tasks.failure_stakes: Lost updates or a corrupt-then-reset state file silently zero out counters that other systems depend on.

key: ignored_errors|config file migration and atomic writes

tasks.title: CSV export to presigned URL
tasks.user_request: Write `export_and_upload(conn, table, url)` that dumps every row of a sqlite table to a CSV file in a temp directory and then PUTs that file to the given presigned URL with requests. It should return the number of rows exported.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must check the HTTP response (raise_for_status or explicit 2xx check) and raise on 4xx/5xx rather than returning the row count; sqlite errors (missing table) must propagate, not be swallowed; the CSV file must be closed/flushed before upload; the temp file should be removed in a finally block; the row count is returned only when the upload succeeded. Tests should mock requests.put returning 403/500 and assert an exception, and assert the count on success.
tasks.failure_stakes: The nightly job logs 'exported 1.2M rows' while the bucket contains nothing, and downstream analytics quietly run on stale data.

tasks.title: Atomic JSON snapshot writer
tasks.user_request: I need `write_snapshot(records, path)` that serializes a list of dicts to JSON at `path`. It runs every 5 minutes and several other processes read that file constantly, so the previous file needs to stay readable until the new one is completely written.
tasks.clean_requirements: Write to a temp file in the same directory, flush and os.fsync, then os.replace onto the target. On any exception (OSError such as ENOSPC, TypeError from a non-serializable value) the temp file must be removed and the exception re-raised, leaving the original file byte-for-byte unchanged. Tests should simulate a failure mid-write (e.g. unserializable record or patched write raising OSError) and assert the original content is intact and no temp files remain.
tasks.failure_stakes: Readers pick up a truncated or half-written JSON file and crash, or the last good snapshot is destroyed when the disk fills up.

tasks.title: pg_dump wrapper
tasks.user_request: Write `dump_database(db_url, out_path)` that shells out to pg_dump and produces a gzipped dump at out_path, returning the size in bytes of the resulting file. We call this before every deploy.
tasks.clean_requirements: Must inspect pg_dump's return code (not just the gzip/pipeline exit status, and not shell=True with a pipe that hides pg_dump failure); include captured stderr in the raised exception; verify the output file exists and is non-trivially sized (more than a bare gzip header) before returning; remove the partial output on failure rather than leaving a truncated dump at out_path. Tests should use a fake pg_dump script on PATH that exits non-zero and assert an exception and no leftover file.
tasks.failure_stakes: A zero-byte or truncated backup overwrites the last good one right before a risky deploy, and there is nothing to restore from.

tasks.title: Chunked CSV parts with manifest
tasks.user_request: Write `export_parts(rows, out_dir, chunk_size=10000)` that writes an iterable of rows into numbered CSV part files (part-00000.csv, part-00001.csv, ...) and finishes by writing manifest.json listing each part and its row count. The downstream loader starts ingesting as soon as the manifest shows up.
tasks.clean_requirements: The manifest must only be written after every part file has been fully written and closed; manifest should be written atomically (temp + rename). If any part fails to write (OSError), already-written parts and the partial part must be deleted and no manifest produced, with the exception propagated. Row counts in the manifest must match actual file contents. Tests should inject a write failure on the Nth part and assert no manifest and no leftover part files, and verify counts on the happy path.
tasks.failure_stakes: The loader ingests a partial dataset as if it were complete, and the missing rows are never noticed.

tasks.title: Deliver export to network share
tasks.user_request: Write `deliver(src_path, dest_dir)` that copies a finished export file onto our mounted network share and then removes the local copy to free disk space. Return the destination path.
tasks.clean_requirements: Copy, then compute a checksum (e.g. sha256) of both source and destination and compare before deleting the source. OSError during copy (ENOSPC, missing dest_dir, permission denied) must remove any partial destination file, keep the source, and raise. The source must never be deleted unless verification passed. Tests should patch shutil.copyfile/copy to write a truncated destination and assert the source still exists and an exception is raised.
tasks.failure_stakes: The local copy is deleted while the copy on the share is truncated by a flaky mount, so the export is simply gone.

tasks.title: Multipart upload client
tasks.user_request: Our storage API does multipart uploads: POST /uploads returns {"id": ...}, PUT /uploads/{id}/parts/{n} takes each chunk, and POST /uploads/{id}/complete finalizes. Write `upload_file(path, base_url, chunk_size=8*1024*1024)` using requests that returns the completed upload id.
tasks.clean_requirements: Every request (initiate, each part, complete) must have its status checked; on a failed part or failed complete, send DELETE /uploads/{id} to abort and raise. Must not call complete if any part failed. Chunks must be read in binary mode and the loop must handle the final short chunk. Tests should mock a 503 on the second part and assert the abort endpoint was called, complete was never called, and an exception was raised; happy path asserts all parts uploaded in order.
tasks.failure_stakes: A half-uploaded object gets finalized and served as a corrupt export, or orphaned parts accumulate storage charges indefinitely.

tasks.title: rsync then mark rows synced
tasks.user_request: Write `sync_exports(local_dir, remote, conn)` that runs `rsync -az local_dir/ remote` and then updates the sqlite `exports` table, setting `synced_at` to now for every row whose `filename` is in local_dir. Return how many rows were marked.
tasks.clean_requirements: Check rsync's return code and raise with stderr on non-zero (treat partial-transfer codes like 23/24 as failure); only run the UPDATE when rsync succeeded; commit on success and rollback on sqlite error; parameterize the SQL rather than interpolating filenames. Tests should use a fake rsync on PATH that exits 23 and assert that no rows were updated and an exception was raised.
tasks.failure_stakes: Rows get marked as synced even though the files never arrived, so they are never retried and quietly vanish from the remote dataset.

tasks.title: JSONL export with webhook trigger
tasks.user_request: Write `export_events(events, path, webhook_url)` that writes the events as JSON lines to `path` and then POSTs `{"path": path, "count": n}` to the webhook so the downstream job kicks off. Return the count.
tasks.clean_requirements: The file must be completely written, flushed, and closed (ideally temp + rename) before the webhook fires; a serialization error or OSError while writing must prevent the webhook call entirely and leave no partial file at `path`. The webhook response must be checked and a non-2xx must raise rather than returning the count. Tests should assert the webhook is not called when writing fails, and that a 500 from the webhook raises.
tasks.failure_stakes: The downstream job is triggered against a missing or half-written file, or the file lands but nobody is ever notified and the pipeline stalls silently.

tasks.title: Archive export directory with system tar
tasks.user_request: Write `archive_exports(src_dir, archive_path)` that tars and gzips everything in `src_dir` into archive_path using the system tar, then deletes the original files to reclaim space. Return the number of files archived.
tasks.clean_requirements: Check tar's return code and raise with stderr on failure; before deleting originals, verify the archive (e.g. `tar -tzf` exits 0 or tarfile lists it) and that the entry count matches the number of source files; delete originals only after verification passes; remove a partial archive on failure; a missing src_dir must raise. Tests should use a fake tar that exits non-zero or writes garbage and assert originals are retained.
tasks.failure_stakes: Originals are deleted while the archive is corrupt or empty, making months of exports unrecoverable.

tasks.title: Incremental export with watermark
tasks.user_request: Write `incremental_export(conn, watermark_file, out_dir, upload_fn)` that reads the last exported `updated_at` from watermark_file, selects rows from `orders` with updated_at greater than it, writes them to a timestamped CSV in out_dir, calls `upload_fn(csv_path)`, and then saves the new high-water mark. Return the number of rows exported.
tasks.clean_requirements: A missing watermark file on first run should be treated as 'export everything', but other OSErrors reading it must raise; the watermark must be advanced only after upload_fn returns successfully, and written atomically; if upload_fn raises, the exception propagates and the watermark file is unchanged; zero new rows should skip the upload and not corrupt the watermark. Tests should pass an upload_fn that raises and assert the watermark file content is unchanged, and check correct advancement on success.
tasks.failure_stakes: The watermark advances after a failed upload, so those orders are permanently skipped from every future export.
